en: The Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines.
Oṃ! Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the earth element does not exist, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.

By way of the emptiness of the earth element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the solitude of the earth element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the earth element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past.
By way of the non-existence of the earth element, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the emptiness of the earth element, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the solitude of the earth element, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By way of the earth element’s lack of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit;
by way of the non-existence of the earth element, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the earth element, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By way of the isolation of the earth element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the earth element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. Why is that?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the earth element, in the emptiness of the earth element, and in the isolation of the earth element—

In the absence of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the earth element, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a posterior limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, the non-existence of the earth element is not other than the emptiness of the earth element; the isolation (*viviktatā*) of the earth element is not other [than it];

the absence of intrinsic nature of the earth element is not other [than it]; the bodhisattva is not other [than it]; the prior limit is not other [than it]; the posterior limit is not other [than it]; and the middle is not other [than it].

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the earth element, that which is the emptiness of the earth element, that which is the solitude of the earth element, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the earth element, and that which is the bodhisattva, and that which is the prior limit, and that which is the subsequent limit, and that which is the middle— all this is non-dual, without division.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of the water element, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by way of the emptiness of the water element, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
by way of the isolation of the water element, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the water element, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
By way of the non-existence of the water element, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;

by way of the emptiness of the water element, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the solitude of the water element, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the water-element having no intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the non-existence of the water-element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the water-element, [a bodhisattva does not approach it] from the middle.
A bodhisattva does not approach;
because the water element is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
because the water element lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. For what reason?
For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the water-element, in the emptiness of the water-element, in the isolation of the water-element,

and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the water-element, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of the water-element one thing, the emptiness of the water-element another, the isolation of the water-element another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the water-element another, and the bodhisattva yet another.
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, for the past limit is one thing, the future limit is another, and the middle is yet another; however, that which is the non-existence of the water element,

the emptiness of the water element, the solitude of the water element, and the lack of intrinsic nature of the water element, as well as the bodhisattva, the past limit, the future limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the fire element does not exist, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because the fire element is empty, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because the fire element is secluded, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
By virtue of the fire element being without intrinsic nature, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit;

by virtue of the non-existence of the fire element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit; by virtue of the emptiness of the fire element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit.
Because the fire element is devoid of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because the fire element lacks self-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because the fire element is non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
Due to the emptiness of the fire element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
due to the seclusion of the fire element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
due to the lack of intrinsic nature of the fire element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?
For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the fire element, in the emptiness of the fire element, in the isolation of the fire element,

and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the fire element, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of the fire element one thing, the emptiness of the fire element another, the isolation of the fire element another, and the lack of intrinsic nature of the fire element another.

"A Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit another, and the middle yet another"— for indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the fire element, that which is the emptiness of the fire element, that which is the solitude of the fire element, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the fire element;
and that which is the Bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the posterior limit, and that which is the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the wind element, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because of the emptiness of the wind element, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because of the solitude of the wind element, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
By way of the intrinsic nature of the wind element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;

by way of the non-existence of the wind element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future; and by way of the emptiness of the wind element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
Due to the isolation of the wind element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
due to the lack of intrinsic nature of the wind element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the non-existence of the wind element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the wind element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the middle;
by way of the solitude of the wind element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the middle.
By way of the intrinsic nature of the wind element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the wind element, in the emptiness of the wind element, in the solitude of the wind element, and in the intrinsic nature of the wind element, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, the non-existence of the wind element is not one thing, the emptiness of the wind element another, the solitude of the wind element another, the intrinsic nature of the wind element another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another. For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the wind element, that which is the emptiness of the wind element, that which is the solitude of the wind element, and that which is the intrinsic nature of the wind element— [these are all identical].
That which is the bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the posterior limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the element of space, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit;
because of the emptiness of the element of space, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.
Due to the isolation of the space-element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit;
due to the lack of intrinsic nature of the space-element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit;
due to the non-existence of the space-element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the subsequent limit.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit by way of the emptiness of the space-element;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit by way of the solitude of the space-element;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the space-element.
By way of the non-existence of the space element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle;

by way of the emptiness of the space element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle; by way of the solitude of the space element, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle.
Because the element of space has no intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the element of space, within the emptiness of the element of space, within the isolation of the element of space, and within the lack of intrinsic nature of the element of space, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the space-element is not one thing, the emptiness of the space-element another, the solitude of the space-element another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the space-element another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another; for indeed, that which is the non-existence of the space-element, that which is the emptiness of the space-element, that which is the solitude of the space-element, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the space-element— [all these are identical].
That which is a bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the subsequent limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and not divided into two.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the element of consciousness (*vijñānadhātu*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit;
because of the emptiness of the element of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.
Because the element of consciousness is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the past;
because the element of consciousness lacks intrinsic nature,
a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the past.
By way of the non-existence of the consciousness element, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;

by way of the emptiness of the consciousness element, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the solitude of the consciousness element, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of the consciousness element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
by virtue of the non-existence of the consciousness element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle;
by virtue of the emptiness of the consciousness element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
Because of the isolation of the consciousness element (*vijñānadhātu*), a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle;
because of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the consciousness element, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. For what reason?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the consciousness element, in the emptiness of the consciousness element, and in the isolation of the consciousness element...

In the absence of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the consciousness element (*vijñānadhātu*), neither a prior limit (*pūrvānta*) is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit (*aparānta*) is apprehended, nor a middle (*madhya*) is apprehended. Furthermore, the non-existence of the consciousness element is not other than the emptiness of the consciousness element; the isolation (*viviktatā*) of the consciousness element is not other [than it];

the absence of intrinsic nature of the consciousness element is not other [than it]; the bodhisattva is not other [than it]; and the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle are each not other [than it].
Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the consciousness element, that which is the emptiness of the consciousness element,

that which is the solitude of the consciousness element, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the consciousness element— along with the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the existence of ignorance, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

by way of the emptiness of ignorance, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the solitude of ignorance, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the past limit by way of the intrinsic nature of ignorance;

a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit by way of the existence of ignorance; a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit by way of the emptiness of ignorance.
A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the isolation of ignorance;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the intrinsic nature of ignorance;
a bodhisattva does not approach the middle through the existence of ignorance.
A bodhisattva does not approach ignorance from the perspective of the middle way by way of its emptiness;
a bodhisattva does not approach ignorance from the perspective of the middle way by way of its seclusion;
a bodhisattva does not approach ignorance from the perspective of the middle way by way of its intrinsic nature. For what reason?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of ignorance, the emptiness of ignorance, the seclusion of ignorance, and the intrinsic nature of ignorance, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is not that the non-existence of ignorance is one thing, the emptiness of ignorance another, the seclusion of ignorance another, the intrinsic nature of ignorance another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another. Thus it is, Venerable Śāradvatīputra.
That which is the existence of ignorance, that which is the emptiness of ignorance, that which is the seclusion of ignorance, that which is the intrinsic nature of ignorance,
the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, due to the non-existence of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
due to the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
due to the solitude of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the past limit;
by way of the non-existence of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the future limit;
by way of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the future limit.
Because conditioned phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
because conditioned phenomena lack self-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
because conditioned phenomena are non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.

By way of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle; by way of the isolation of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. For what reason?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the isolation of conditioned phenomena, and the lack of intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of conditioned phenomena one thing, and the emptiness of conditioned phenomena another, and the isolation of conditioned phenomena another, and the lack of intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena another.

"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit another; yet that which is the non-existence of conditioned phenomena, that which is the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, that which is the seclusion of conditioned phenomena, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena— along with the Bodhisattva, the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible."

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the emptiness of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the solitude of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness, one does not approach a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;

by way of the non-existence of consciousness, one does not approach a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future; by way of the emptiness of consciousness, one does not approach a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
By way of the isolation of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the non-existence of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the isolation of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of consciousness, in the emptiness of consciousness, in the isolation of consciousness, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Nor is there anything other than the non-existence of consciousness, anything other than the emptiness of consciousness, anything other than the isolation of consciousness, or anything other than the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness.

"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit another; yet that which is the non-existence of consciousness, that which is the emptiness of consciousness, that which is the isolation of consciousness, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness— along with the Bodhisattva, the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of name-and-form, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because of the emptiness of name-and-form, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because of the solitude of name-and-form, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of name-and-form, a bodhisattva does not approach [the bodhisattva] from the perspective of the past; by way of the non-existence of name-and-form, a bodhisattva does not approach [the bodhisattva] from the perspective of the future; by way of the emptiness of name-and-form, a bodhisattva does not approach [the bodhisattva] from the perspective of the future.
By way of the seclusion of name-and-form, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of name-and-form, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the non-existence of name-and-form, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the middle.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the emptiness of name-and-form;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the seclusion of name-and-form;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of name-and-form. Why is that?
For indeed, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of name-and-form, in the emptiness of name-and-form, in the solitude of name-and-form,

and in the lack of intrinsic nature of name-and-form, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of name-and-form one thing, the emptiness of name-and-form another, the solitude of name-and-form another, and the lack of intrinsic nature of name-and-form another.

"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit another; yet that which is the existence of name-and-form, that which is the emptiness of name-and-form, that which is the solitude of name-and-form, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of name-and-form, the bodhisattva himself, the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of the six sense bases, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

by way of the emptiness of the six sense bases, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; and by way of the solitude of the six sense bases, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the six sense bases, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;

by way of the non-existence of the six sense bases, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future; and by way of the emptiness of the six sense bases, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
By virtue of the seclusion of the six sense bases, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
by virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of the six sense bases, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
and by virtue of the non-existence of the six sense bases, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of the six sense-bases, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the seclusion of the six sense-bases, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the six sense-bases, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the six sense bases, the emptiness of the six sense bases, the isolation of the six sense bases, and the lack of intrinsic nature of the six sense bases, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of the six sense bases one thing, and the emptiness of the six sense bases another, and the isolation of the six sense bases another, and the lack of intrinsic nature of the six sense bases another.
The Bodhisattva is one thing, the past limit another, and the future limit another, and the middle yet another; for, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the six sense bases,
that which is the emptiness of the six sense bases, that which is the solitude of the six sense bases, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the six sense bases— [is the Bodhisattva].
And the bodhisattva, whatever is the past limit, whatever is the future limit, and whatever is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Because of the non-existence of contact, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past limit;
because of the emptiness of contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past limit.
By way of the isolation of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past; by way of the non-existence of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.
By way of the emptiness of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the isolation of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By way of the non-existence of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle; by way of the isolation of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of contact, the emptiness of contact, the isolation of contact, and the lack of intrinsic nature of contact, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of contact is not one thing, the emptiness of contact another, the isolation of contact another, the lack of intrinsic nature of contact another, and the bodhisattva another; nor is the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another.

For indeed, that which is the non-existence of contact, that which is the emptiness of contact, that which is the isolation of contact, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of contact, and that which is the bodhisattva—[these are not different].
That which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because feeling does not exist, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit;
because feeling is empty, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit.
By way of the isolation of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
by way of the intrinsic nature of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past; by way of the non-existence of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.
By way of the emptiness of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the solitude of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the intrinsic nature of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.

A bodhisattva does not approach feeling from the perspective of the middle by way of the existence of feeling, nor does he approach it from the perspective of the middle by way of the emptiness of feeling,
nor does he approach it from the perspective of the middle by way of the solitude of feeling.
By way of the intrinsic nature of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, neither a prior limit, nor a subsequent limit, nor a middle is perceived in the existence of feeling, in the emptiness of feeling, in the solitude of feeling, or in the intrinsic nature of feeling.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of feeling is not one thing, the emptiness of feeling another, the solitude of feeling another, the lack of intrinsic nature of feeling another, and the Bodhisattva another;

nor is the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another. For indeed, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of feeling, that which is the emptiness of feeling, that which is the solitude of feeling, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of feeling, and that which is the Bodhisattva—[these are not distinct].
That which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the existence of craving, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past limit;
by way of the emptiness of craving, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past limit.
By way of being secluded from craving, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
by way of the intrinsic nature of craving, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past; by way of the non-existence of craving, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.
By way of the emptiness of craving, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the seclusion of craving, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the intrinsic nature of craving, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.

A bodhisattva does not approach craving from the perspective of its existence as being intermediate; a bodhisattva does not approach craving from the perspective of its emptiness as being intermediate;
a bodhisattva does not approach craving from the perspective of its isolation as being intermediate.
By way of the intrinsic nature of craving, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the existence of craving, in the emptiness of craving, in the seclusion of craving, and in the intrinsic nature of craving, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

The existence of craving is not one thing, the emptiness of craving another, the solitude of craving another, the intrinsic nature of craving another, and the bodhisattva another; nor is the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another. For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of craving, that which is the emptiness of craving, that which is the solitude of craving, that which is the intrinsic nature of craving, and that which is the bodhisattva—[these are not distinct].
That which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because grasping does not exist, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
because grasping is empty, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
Because of the isolation of grasping, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

because of the lack of intrinsic nature of grasping, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the non-existence of grasping, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.
By way of the emptiness of grasping, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the solitude of grasping, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of grasping, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
Because of the non-existence of grasping, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
because of the emptiness of grasping, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle; because of the isolation of grasping, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of grasping, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

Because, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of grasping, the emptiness of grasping, the seclusion of grasping, and the lack of intrinsic nature of grasping, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, the non-existence of appropriation is not one thing, the emptiness of appropriation another, the isolation of appropriation another, the lack of intrinsic nature of appropriation another,

the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another. For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of appropriation and that which is the emptiness of appropriation— [they are not different].

That which is the state of being devoid of grasping, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature in grasping, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Because of the non-existence of becoming, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.

By way of the emptiness of existence, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the isolation of existence, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of existence, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past.
By way of the non-existence of existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the emptiness of existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the isolation of existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of existence, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the non-existence of existence, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle;
by way of the emptiness of existence, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the seclusion of existence, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of existence, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. For what reason?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of existence, in the emptiness of existence, and in the seclusion of existence—

In the absence of intrinsic nature in existence (*bhavāsvabhāvatā*), neither a prior limit (*pūrvānta*) is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit (*aparānta*) is apprehended, nor a middle (*madhya*) is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of existence is not one thing, the emptiness of existence another, the isolation of existence another, the absence of intrinsic nature in existence another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another; for that which is the non-existence of existence...

That which is the emptiness of existence, that which is the seclusion of existence, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of existence; and that which is the bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the subsequent limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Because birth is non-existent, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.

By way of the emptiness of birth, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the isolation of birth, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of birth, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the non-existence of birth; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the emptiness of birth;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the solitude of birth.

By way of the absence of intrinsic nature in birth, a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the non-existence of birth, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of birth, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle.
By way of the isolation of birth, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle; by way of the absence of intrinsic nature in birth, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?
For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of birth, in the emptiness of birth, in the isolation of birth, and in the absence of intrinsic nature in birth—

The prior limit is not apprehended, the posterior limit is not apprehended, and the middle is not apprehended. Furthermore, the non-existence of birth is not one thing, the emptiness of birth another, the isolation of birth another, the lack of intrinsic nature of birth another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another; for indeed—
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of birth, that which is the emptiness of birth, that which is the solitude of birth,
that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of birth, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—
all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of old age and death, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;

because of the emptiness of old age and death, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; because of the solitude of old age and death, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of aging and death, a bodhisattva does not approach [them] from the perspective of the past limit;

by virtue of the non-existence (*asattā*) of aging and death, a bodhisattva does not approach [them] from the perspective of the future limit; by virtue of the emptiness (*śūnyatā*) of aging and death, a bodhisattva does not approach [them] from the perspective of the future limit.
Because of the isolation of old age and death, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
because of the lack of intrinsic nature of old age and death, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
because of the non-existence of old age and death, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of old age and death, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of old age and death, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of old age and death, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. For what reason?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of old age and death, within the emptiness of old age and death, within the isolation of old age and death, and within the intrinsic nature of old age and death, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of old age and death one thing, the emptiness of old age and death another, the isolation of old age and death another, and the intrinsic nature of old age and death another.
The Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit another, and the middle yet another—thus it is, venerable Śāradvatīputra.

For that which is the non-existence of old age and death, that which is the emptiness of old age and death, that which is the solitude of old age and death, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of old age and death;
and that which is the Bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the posterior limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the existence of the perfection of generosity, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the emptiness of the perfection of generosity, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by way of the solitude of the perfection of generosity, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the prior limit; by way of the non-existence of the perfection of generosity, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the posterior limit;
by way of the emptiness of the perfection of generosity, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the posterior limit.
Because the perfection of generosity is isolated, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;

because the perfection of generosity has the nature of intrinsic being, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit; because the perfection of generosity lacks substantial existence, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
A bodhisattva does not approach the perfection of generosity from the perspective of the middle way by way of the emptiness of the perfection of generosity;
a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle way by way of the solitude of the perfection of generosity;
a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle way by way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity. Why is that?

For indeed, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the existence of the perfection of generosity, in the emptiness of the perfection of generosity, in the solitude of the perfection of generosity, and in the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a posterior limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. And the existence of the perfection of generosity is not other than the emptiness of the perfection of generosity, nor is it other [than that].

The seclusion of the perfection of generosity is one thing, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity is another, the bodhisattva is another, the prior limit is another, the posterior limit is another, and the middle is yet another. For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of the perfection of generosity, that which is the emptiness of the perfection of generosity, that which is the seclusion of the perfection of generosity, and that which is the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity—[is all this not one and the same? That which is...
And the bodhisattva, as well as the past limit, the future limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit;
by way of the emptiness of the perfection of ethical discipline, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit.
By way of the isolation of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

by way of the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the perfection of ethical discipline, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; and by way of the existence of the perfection of ethical discipline, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.
By way of the emptiness of the perfection of ethical discipline, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the seclusion of the perfection of ethical discipline, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of ethical discipline, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit.

By way of the existence of the perfection of ethical discipline, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle; by way of the emptiness of the perfection of ethical discipline, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle;
by way of the solitude of the perfection of ethical discipline, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of ethical discipline, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of the perfection of ethical discipline, within the emptiness of the perfection of ethical discipline, within the solitude of the perfection of ethical discipline, and within the intrinsic nature of the perfection of ethical discipline, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of the perfection of ethical discipline is not one thing, the emptiness of the perfection of ethical discipline another, the solitude of the perfection of ethical discipline another, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of ethical discipline another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. For indeed,

that which is the existence of the perfection of ethical discipline, that which is the emptiness of the perfection of ethical discipline, and that which is the solitude of the perfection of ethical discipline— [are all one].

And the intrinsic nature of the perfection of ethical discipline, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the non-existence of the perfection of patience, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of the perfection of patience, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;
by way of the solitude of the perfection of patience, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of patience, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past.

By way of the existence of the perfection of patience, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the emptiness of the perfection of patience, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the solitude of the perfection of patience, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of patience, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit;
by way of the existence of the perfection of patience, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the perfection of patience, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By way of the seclusion of the perfection of patience, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of patience, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is no existence of the perfection of patience, no emptiness of the perfection of patience, and no seclusion of the perfection of patience.

In the intrinsic nature of the perfection of patience, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, the existence of the perfection of patience is not one thing, its emptiness another, its solitude another, its intrinsic nature another,
the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of the perfection of patience, the emptiness of the perfection of patience, the solitude of the perfection of patience, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of patience, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of the perfection of vigor, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by virtue of the emptiness of the perfection of vigor, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by virtue of the solitude of the perfection of vigor, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By virtue of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of vigor, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by virtue of the non-existence of the perfection of vigor, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; and by virtue of the emptiness of the perfection of vigor, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.
Because the perfection of vigor is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because the perfection of vigor has the nature of selflessness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because the perfection of vigor lacks intrinsic existence, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of the perfection of vigor, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of the perfection of vigor, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of vigor, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?
For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of the perfection of vigor, the emptiness of the perfection of vigor, the solitude of the perfection of vigor,

and the intrinsic nature of the perfection of vigor, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Nor is the existence of the perfection of vigor one thing, its emptiness another, its solitude another, and its intrinsic nature yet another.

"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of vigor is not one thing, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another. For that which is the existence of the perfection of vigor, that which is the emptiness of the perfection of vigor,
that which is the solitude of the perfection of vigor, that which is the intrinsic nature of the perfection of vigor, and that which is the bodhisattva— "
And that which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the non-existence of the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past limit;
through the emptiness of the perfection of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past limit.
Due to the isolation of the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*),
a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
due to the intrinsic nature of the perfection of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By way of the existence of the perfection of meditation, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the emptiness of the perfection of meditation, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the solitude of the perfection of meditation, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit;
by way of the existence of the perfection of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the perfection of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.

By virtue of the seclusion of the perfection of meditation, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. By virtue of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of meditation, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, neither a prior limit nor a subsequent limit nor a middle is apprehended in the existence of the perfection of meditation, in the emptiness of the perfection of meditation, in the seclusion of the perfection of meditation, or in the intrinsic nature of the perfection of meditation.

It is perceived. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of the perfection of meditation is not one thing, the emptiness of the perfection of meditation another, the solitude of the perfection of meditation another, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of meditation another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another. For indeed, that which is the existence of the perfection of meditation and that which is the emptiness of the perfection of meditation [are not different].

The seclusion of the perfection of meditative concentration and the intrinsic nature of the perfection of meditative concentration, as well as the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the non-existence of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva does not come from the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit;

by way of the solitude of the perfection of wisdom, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit; by way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit.

By way of the existence of the perfection of wisdom, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the solitude of the perfection of wisdom, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit;
by way of the non-existence of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By virtue of the seclusion of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
by virtue of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. For what reason?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the existence of the perfection of wisdom, in the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, and in the seclusion of the perfection of wisdom—

In the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom, a prior limit is not apprehended, a subsequent limit is not apprehended, and a middle is not apprehended. Furthermore, the existence of the perfection of wisdom is not other than the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom; the isolation of the perfection of wisdom is not other [than it];

the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom is not other [than it]; the bodhisattva is not other [than it]; the prior limit is not other [than it]; the subsequent limit is not other [than it]; and the middle is not other [than it].

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the perfection of wisdom, that which is the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, that which is the solitude of the perfection of wisdom,

that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom, and that which is the bodhisattva, and that which is the prior limit, and that which is the subsequent limit— [all these are not two, nor are they distinct].
And all this middle is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the existence of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit;
by way of the emptiness of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit.
By virtue of the seclusion of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;

by virtue of the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past; by virtue of the existence of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.
By way of the emptiness of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the seclusion of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By way of the existence of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the isolation of internal emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By virtue of having internal emptiness as its intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of internal emptiness, within the emptiness of internal emptiness, within the solitude of internal emptiness, and within the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

It is perceived. Furthermore, the existence of internal emptiness is not one thing, the emptiness of internal emptiness another, the seclusion of internal emptiness another, the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of internal emptiness, that which is the emptiness of internal emptiness, and that which is the seclusion of internal emptiness—[are all one].
That which is the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness, that which is the bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the subsequent limit, and that which is the middle—
all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of external emptiness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of external emptiness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;

by way of the solitude of external emptiness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the intrinsic nature of external emptiness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past.
A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the existence of external emptiness; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the emptiness of external emptiness;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the solitude of external emptiness.

By virtue of the intrinsic nature of external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit; by virtue of the existence of external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle; by virtue of the emptiness of external emptiness—(ŚsP_II-1_15) —[a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the past limit].
A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
because of the seclusion of external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
because of the intrinsic nature of external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. For what reason?
For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of external emptiness, within the emptiness of external emptiness, within the solitude of external emptiness,

and within the intrinsic nature of external emptiness, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended. Nor is the existence of external emptiness one thing, the emptiness of external emptiness another, the solitude of external emptiness another, [and the intrinsic nature of external emptiness yet another.]
The intrinsic nature of external emptiness is not one thing, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle yet another.

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of external emptiness, that which is the emptiness of external emptiness, that which is the solitude of external emptiness, that which is the intrinsic nature of external emptiness, and that which is the bodhisattva— [all these are not different].
That which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā*), a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the past limit;
by virtue of the emptiness of internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatāśūnyatā*), a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the past limit.
Due to the isolation of internal-external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
due to the intrinsic nature of internal-external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
due to the non-existence of internal-external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.
By way of the emptiness of the emptiness of internal and external [phenomena], a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the solitude of the emptiness of internal and external [phenomena], a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of internal and external [phenomena], a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By way of the existence of internal-and-external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of internal-and-external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of internal-and-external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By virtue of the intrinsic nature of internal-external emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. For what reason?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is no prior limit in the existence of internal-external emptiness, in the emptiness of internal-external emptiness, in the isolation of internal-external emptiness, or in the intrinsic nature of internal-external emptiness.

Neither a posterior limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, the existence of internal-and-external emptiness is not other than the emptiness of internal-and-external emptiness, nor is it other than the isolation of internal-and-external emptiness, nor is it other than the intrinsic nature of internal-and-external emptiness; nor is the bodhisattva other, nor the prior limit other, nor the posterior limit other, nor the middle other. For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of internal-and-external emptiness, that which is the emptiness of internal-and-external emptiness, and that which is the isolation of internal-and-external emptiness—[are all one].

That which is the intrinsic nature of internal-and-external emptiness, that which is the bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the subsequent limit, and that which is the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the prior limit.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit by way of the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness;

a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit by way of the seclusion of the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness; a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness.

A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the existence of the emptiness of emptiness; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the isolation of the emptiness of emptiness.
By virtue of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle;
by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
Because of the emptiness and seclusion of the emptiness of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
because of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. For what reason?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is no existence of the emptiness of emptiness, no emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness, and no seclusion of the emptiness of emptiness.

In the essential nature of the emptiness of emptiness, a prior limit is not apprehended, a subsequent limit is not apprehended, and a middle is not apprehended. Furthermore, the existence of the emptiness of emptiness is not other than the emptiness of emptiness;

the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness is not other [than it]; the seclusion of the emptiness of emptiness is not other [than it]; the essential nature of the emptiness of emptiness is not other [than it]; the bodhisattva is not other [than it]; the prior limit is not other [than it]; the subsequent limit is not other [than it]; and the middle is not other [than it].

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of the emptiness of emptiness, that which is the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness, that which is the solitude of the emptiness of emptiness, that which is the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of emptiness, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of great emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by virtue of the emptiness of great emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by virtue of the solitude of great emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By virtue of the intrinsic nature of great emptiness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit; by virtue of the existence of great emptiness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit; by virtue of the emptiness of great emptiness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit.
Due to the isolation of great emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;

due to the intrinsic nature of great emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; due to the non-existence of great emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of great emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of great emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the intrinsic nature of great emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of great emptiness, within the emptiness of great emptiness, within the solitude of great emptiness, and within the intrinsic nature of great emptiness, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended.
Nor is the existence of great emptiness one thing and [the aforementioned] another.

The emptiness of great emptiness is one thing, the solitude of great emptiness is another, the intrinsic nature of great emptiness is another, and the bodhisattva is another; the prior limit is another, the posterior limit is another, and the middle is another. For, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of great emptiness, that which is the emptiness of great emptiness, that which is the solitude of great emptiness, that which is the intrinsic nature of great emptiness, and that which is the bodhisattva—[these are not different].
And the Bodhisattva, that which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Because of the existence of ultimate emptiness, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one does not apprehend a Bodhisattva from the past limit;
because of the emptiness of ultimate emptiness, one does not apprehend a Bodhisattva from the past limit.
Because ultimate emptiness is secluded, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

because ultimate emptiness is the intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because ultimate emptiness exists, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

By way of the emptiness of ultimate reality being empty, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the ultimate reality being secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the ultimate reality having the nature of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the existence of ultimate emptiness; a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the emptiness of ultimate emptiness;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the isolation of ultimate emptiness.
By virtue of having ultimate emptiness as its intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, neither a prior limit is perceived in the existence of ultimate emptiness, nor in the emptiness of ultimate emptiness, nor in the seclusion of ultimate emptiness, nor in the intrinsic nature of ultimate emptiness.

Neither the future limit is apprehended nor the middle is apprehended. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of ultimate emptiness is not one thing, the emptiness of ultimate emptiness another, the seclusion of ultimate emptiness another, the intrinsic nature of ultimate emptiness another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the future limit another, and the middle another. Such is the case, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.

That which is the existence of ultimate emptiness, that which is the emptiness of ultimate emptiness, that which is the solitude of ultimate emptiness, that which is the intrinsic nature of ultimate emptiness, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because conditioned emptiness exists, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because conditioned emptiness is empty, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because conditioned emptiness is secluded, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
Because conditioned phenomena are empty by nature, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the past;

because conditioned phenomena exist as empty, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future; and because conditioned phenomena are empty of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future.
Because conditioned emptiness is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;

because conditioned emptiness has the nature of intrinsic being, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit; because conditioned emptiness lacks substantial existence, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena being empty, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the seclusion of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of conditioned emptiness, within the emptiness of conditioned emptiness, within the seclusion of conditioned emptiness, and within the intrinsic nature of conditioned emptiness, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, the existence of conditioned emptiness is not one thing, the emptiness of conditioned emptiness another, the seclusion of conditioned emptiness another, and [its intrinsic nature] yet another.

"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is because the nature of the emptiness of the conditioned is not one thing and the bodhisattva another, nor the prior limit another, nor the subsequent limit another, nor the middle another. For indeed, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of the emptiness of the conditioned,

that which is the emptiness of the emptiness of the conditioned, that which is the solitude of the emptiness of the conditioned, that which is the nature of the emptiness of the conditioned, and that which is the bodhisattva— "
That which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the existence of the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the past limit;
because of the emptiness of the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the past limit.
Due to the seclusion of the emptiness of the unconditioned, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
due to the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the unconditioned, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
due to the existence of the emptiness of the unconditioned, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.
By way of the emptiness of the unconditioned, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;

by way of the seclusion of the emptiness of the unconditioned, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the unconditioned, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By way of the existence of the emptiness of the unconditioned, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the emptiness of the unconditioned, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of the emptiness of the unconditioned, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By virtue of having unconditioned emptiness as its intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of unconditioned emptiness, within the emptiness of unconditioned emptiness, within the seclusion of unconditioned emptiness, and within the intrinsic nature of unconditioned emptiness, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

It is perceived. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of the emptiness of the unconditioned is not one thing, the emptiness of the emptiness of the unconditioned another, the seclusion of the emptiness of the unconditioned another, the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the unconditioned another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another.

For indeed, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of the emptiness of the unconditioned, that which is the emptiness of the emptiness of the unconditioned, and that which is the seclusion of the emptiness of the unconditioned—[are all one].
That which is the nature of the emptiness of the unconditioned, that which is the bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the subsequent limit,
and that which is the middle— all this is non-dual, without division.
