Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

by virtue of the emptiness of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past. By virtue of the isolation of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by virtue of the intrinsic nature of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
By way of the existence of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the emptiness of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the solitude of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By virtue of the intrinsic nature of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit;
by virtue of the existence of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by virtue of the emptiness of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
Because of the isolation of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
because of the intrinsic nature of absolute emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is no such thing as the existence of absolute emptiness, the emptiness of absolute emptiness, or the isolation of absolute emptiness.
In the intrinsic nature of absolute emptiness, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of absolute emptiness is not one thing, the emptiness of absolute emptiness another, the isolation of absolute emptiness another, the intrinsic nature of absolute emptiness another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. Thus it is, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.
The existence of absolute emptiness, the emptiness of absolute emptiness, the isolation of absolute emptiness,
the intrinsic nature of absolute emptiness, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the existence of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit;
because of the emptiness of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit;
because of the solitude of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.

By virtue of having beginningless and endless emptiness as its intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit. By virtue of the existence of beginningless and endless emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit. By virtue of the emptiness of beginningless and endless emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit. By virtue of the isolation of beginningless and endless emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit. By virtue of the intrinsic nature of beginningless and endless emptiness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit.

A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the existence of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*). A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the emptiness of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end. A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the isolation of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end. A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end. For what reason?
For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of the beginningless and endless emptiness (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*),

within the emptiness of the beginningless and endless emptiness, within the isolation of the beginningless and endless emptiness, and within the intrinsic nature of the beginningless and endless emptiness— which is neither other than the emptiness of the beginningless and endless emptiness nor other than the isolation of the beginningless and endless emptiness— there is no Bodhisattva who is one thing, and the prior limit (*pūrvānta*) another, the posterior limit (*aparānta*) another, and the middle (*madhya*) another. For it is thus, Venerable Śāradvatīputra.
The existence of beginningless and endless emptiness, the emptiness of beginningless and endless emptiness, the solitude of beginningless and endless emptiness,
the intrinsic nature of beginningless and endless emptiness, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of non-dispersal, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit;
and by virtue of the solitude of the emptiness of non-dispersal, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.
By virtue of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit;

by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of non-dispersal, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit; and by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of non-dispersal, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit.
Because non-dispersal emptiness is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because non-dispersal emptiness has the nature of intrinsic being, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because non-dispersal emptiness lacks substantial existence, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of the emptiness of non-dispersal, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-dispersal, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?
For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of non-repudiation emptiness, within the emptiness of non-repudiation emptiness, within the isolation of non-repudiation emptiness,

and within the intrinsic nature of non-repudiation emptiness, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended. Nor is the existence of non-repudiation emptiness one thing, the emptiness of non-repudiation emptiness another, the isolation of non-repudiation emptiness another, and the intrinsic nature of non-repudiation emptiness yet another.
"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit is another, and the posterior limit is yet another.

For that which is the existence of the emptiness of non-dispersal (anavakāra-śūnyatā), that which is the emptiness of the emptiness of non-dispersal, that which is the solitude of the emptiness of non-dispersal,
that which is the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-dispersal, and that which is the Bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, and that which is the posterior limit— "
And all this middle is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
Due to the solitude of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
due to the self-nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
due to the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.

By way of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the seclusion of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the self-nature of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
A bodhisattva does not approach intrinsic emptiness as a real entity; because intrinsic emptiness is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because intrinsic emptiness is the very nature of things, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By virtue of having the nature of emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā-svabhāvatā*), a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, in the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, in the isolation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and in the nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither a prior limit (*pūrvānta*) is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit (*aparānta*) is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

It is perceived. Furthermore, the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not one thing, the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature another, the seclusion of the emptiness of intrinsic nature another, the self-nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature and that which is the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature—[they are not different].

That which is the emptiness of intrinsic nature, that which is the solitude of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, that which is the self-nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible. Because of the non-existence of the emptiness of all phenomena, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of the emptiness of all dharmas, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit;
by way of the seclusion of the emptiness of all dharmas, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of all dharmas, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit.
By way of the existence of the emptiness of all dharmas, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the emptiness of the emptiness of all dharmas, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the solitude of the emptiness of all dharmas, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
Because all phenomena have the nature of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
because all phenomena exist as emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
and because all phenomena are empty of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
Because of the emptiness and solitude of all dharmas, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
because of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of all dharmas, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?
For, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the existence of the emptiness of all dharmas, and in the emptiness of the emptiness of all dharmas—

In the emptiness and solitude of all phenomena, and in the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of all phenomena, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, the existence of the emptiness of all phenomena is not other than the emptiness of the emptiness of all phenomena; it is not other than the solitude of the emptiness of all phenomena; it is not other than the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of all phenomena.
"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another,

and the subsequent limit another; indeed, that which is the existence of the emptiness of all phenomena, that which is the emptiness of the emptiness of all phenomena, that which is the solitude of the emptiness of all phenomena,
that which is the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of all phenomena, and that which is the Bodhisattva— [all these are distinct]."
That which is the past limit, the future limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the existence of the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; because of the emptiness of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
Because of the solitude of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

because of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the existence of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.
By way of the emptiness of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the solitude of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By way of the existence of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the isolation of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By virtue of having the nature of the emptiness of specific characteristics, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, neither the existence of the emptiness of specific characteristics, nor the emptiness of the emptiness of specific characteristics, nor the seclusion of the emptiness of specific characteristics, nor the nature of the emptiness of specific characteristics is apprehended at the prior limit.

Neither the future limit is apprehended nor the middle is apprehended. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of the emptiness of specific characteristics is not one thing, the emptiness of the emptiness of specific characteristics another, the isolation of the emptiness of specific characteristics another, the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of specific characteristics another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the future limit another, and the middle another. Thus it is, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.
The existence of the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of the emptiness of specific characteristics, the isolation of the emptiness of specific characteristics,
the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of specific characteristics, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of non-apprehension, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of non-apprehension, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
by virtue of the solitude of the emptiness of non-apprehension, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.

By virtue of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-apprehension, one does not find a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of non-apprehension, one does not find a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future; and by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of non-apprehension, one does not find a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
Because of the solitude of the emptiness of non-apprehension, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;
because of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-apprehension, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;
because of the existence of the emptiness of non-apprehension, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of non-apprehension, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of the emptiness of non-apprehension, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-apprehension, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of non-apprehension-emptiness, within the emptiness of non-apprehension-emptiness, within the seclusion of non-apprehension-emptiness, and within the intrinsic nature of non-apprehension-emptiness, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended. Nor is the existence of non-apprehension-emptiness one thing, and the emptiness of non-apprehension-emptiness another, and the seclusion of non-apprehension-emptiness another, and the intrinsic nature of non-apprehension-emptiness another.

"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit is another, and the posterior limit is another. For that which is the existence of the emptiness of non-apprehension, that which is the emptiness of the emptiness of non-apprehension, that which is the solitude of the emptiness of non-apprehension,

that which is the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-apprehension, and that which is the Bodhisattva, and that which is the prior limit, and that which is the posterior limit— [all these are distinct]."
And that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.
By virtue of the solitude of the emptiness of non-existence, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;

by virtue of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-existence, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; and by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of non-existence, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
By way of the emptiness of non-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;

by way of the solitude of the emptiness of non-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit. By way of the existence of the emptiness of non-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle.
By way of the emptiness of non-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle;
by way of the solitude of the emptiness of non-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle. Why is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of the emptiness of non-existence, within the emptiness of the emptiness of non-existence, within the isolation of the emptiness of non-existence, and within the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-existence, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Nor is the existence of the emptiness of non-existence other than the emptiness of the emptiness of non-existence, nor other than the isolation of the emptiness of non-existence, nor other than the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-existence.
"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit another, and the middle yet another. For indeed,

that which is the existence of the emptiness of non-existence, that which is the emptiness of the emptiness of non-existence, that which is the solitude of the emptiness of non-existence, and that which is the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-existence— along with the Bodhisattva, the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible."

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
and by way of the seclusion of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By virtue of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by virtue of the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; and by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit.

By virtue of the solitude of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach awakening from the perspective of the future; by virtue of the solitude of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach [awakening] from the perspective of the middle.
By virtue of having the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, neither a prior limit, nor a subsequent limit, nor a middle is apprehended in the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, in the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, in the seclusion of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or in the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

It is perceived. Furthermore, the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not one thing, the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature another, the isolation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature another, the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature and that which is the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature—[are they different?]

That which is the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), the solitude of intrinsic nature, and the very nature of intrinsic nature; that which is the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Because of the existence of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva does not approach from the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit;
by way of the solitude of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit;
by way of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit.

A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the existence of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the emptiness of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the solitude of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

By virtue of having non-existence-as-own-nature emptiness as its own-nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit; by virtue of the existence of non-existence-as-own-nature emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by virtue of the emptiness of non-existence-as-own-nature emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.

A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle because of the seclusion of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle because of the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Why is that?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, there is no existence of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, nor is there any emptiness of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

In the seclusion of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and in the essential nature of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is not one thing, the emptiness of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence another, the seclusion of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence another, the essential nature of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. Thus it is, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.
The existence of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, the emptiness of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, the isolation of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence,
the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is [identical].
It is non-dual and without division.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because of the emptiness of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
Because of the seclusion of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
because of the lack of intrinsic nature of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;
because of the non-existence of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.
By way of the emptiness of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;

by way of the seclusion of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the non-existence of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
by way of the isolation of the applications of mindfulness, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?

For, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the foundations of mindfulness, within the emptiness of the foundations of mindfulness, within the isolation of the foundations of mindfulness, and within the lack of intrinsic nature of the foundations of mindfulness, neither a prior limit (*pūrvānta*) is apprehended, nor a later limit (*aparānta*) is apprehended, nor a middle (*madhya*) is apprehended.

It is perceived. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the applications of mindfulness is not one thing, the emptiness of the applications of mindfulness another, the isolation of the applications of mindfulness another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the applications of mindfulness another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another. For indeed, that which is the non-existence of the applications of mindfulness and that which is the emptiness of the applications of mindfulness—[are these two different things?]

That which is the seclusion of the applications of mindfulness, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the applications of mindfulness, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the right efforts, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of the right efforts, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by way of the solitude of the right efforts, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the right efforts, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
Because of the non-existence of the right efforts, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
because of the emptiness of the right efforts, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
because of the solitude of the right efforts, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the right efforts, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the non-existence of the right efforts, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the right efforts, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
Because of the seclusion of the right efforts, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
because of the lack of intrinsic nature of the right efforts, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. For what reason?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the right efforts, in the emptiness of the right efforts, in the seclusion of the right efforts, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the right efforts—

The prior limit is not apprehended, the subsequent limit is not apprehended, and the middle is not apprehended. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the right efforts is not one thing, the emptiness of the right efforts another, the solitude of the right efforts another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the right efforts another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another; for indeed, that which is the non-existence of the right efforts—
That which is the emptiness of the right efforts, that which is the solitude of the right efforts, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the right efforts—
along with the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Because of the non-existence of the bases of psychic power, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of the bases of psychic power, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;
by way of the seclusion of the bases of psychic power, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past.
By way of the non-existence of the bases of psychic power, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the emptiness of the bases of psychic power, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit;

by way of the solitude of the bases of psychic power, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the non-existence of the bases of psychic power;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the emptiness of the bases of psychic power;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the solitude of the bases of psychic power.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the bases of psychic power, in the emptiness of the bases of psychic power, in the solitude of the bases of psychic power, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a later limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

The non-existence of the bases of psychic power is not one thing, the emptiness of the bases of psychic power another, the isolation of the bases of psychic power another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle yet another. For, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the bases of psychic power, that which is the emptiness of the bases of psychic power, that which is the isolation of the bases of psychic power, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power— [these are all identical].
That which is a bodhisattva, that which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the sense faculties do not exist, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit;
because the sense faculties are empty, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit.
By virtue of the seclusion of the faculties, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

by virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of the faculties, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by virtue of the non-existence of the faculties, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

By way of the emptiness of the faculties, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the seclusion of the faculties, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the faculties, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the non-existence of the faculties, does not approach from the middle by way of the emptiness of the faculties,
and does not approach from the middle by way of the solitude of the faculties.
By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of the faculties, the bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the faculties, in the emptiness of the faculties, and in the isolation of the faculties—
In the absence of intrinsic nature in the sense faculties, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the sense faculties is not other than the emptiness of the sense faculties; the isolation of the sense faculties is not other [than that]; the absence of intrinsic nature in the sense faculties is not other [than that];
and the bodhisattva is not other [than that]; nor is the prior limit other, the subsequent limit other, or the middle other. Thus it is, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.

That which is the non-existence of the faculties, that which is the emptiness of the faculties, that which is the seclusion of the faculties, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the faculties,

and the bodhisattva, and the prior limit, and the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and not divided into two. Because of the non-existence of the powers, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the prior limit.

By way of the emptiness of the powers, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the isolation of the powers, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the powers, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the existence of the powers; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the emptiness of the powers; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the isolation of the powers.

By way of the intrinsic nature of the powers, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the non-existence of the powers, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the powers, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.

By way of the isolation of the powers (*bala*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the powers, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle. Why is that?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the powers, in the emptiness of the powers, in the isolation of the powers, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the powers—

The prior limit is not apprehended, the posterior limit is not apprehended, and the middle is not apprehended. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the powers is not one thing, the emptiness of the powers another, the isolation of the powers another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the powers another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another; for indeed, that which is the non-existence of the powers and that which is the emptiness of the powers [are not different].
That which is the powerlessness of the powers, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the powers, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—
all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the factors of enlightenment are non-existent, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.

By way of the emptiness of the factors of enlightenment, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the seclusion of the factors of enlightenment, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the factors of enlightenment, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past.

By way of the non-existence of the factors of enlightenment, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the emptiness of the factors of enlightenment, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the solitude of the factors of enlightenment, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the factors of enlightenment, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the non-existence of the factors of enlightenment, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the factors of enlightenment, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
Because the factors of enlightenment are devoid of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
because the factors of enlightenment lack an inherent self-nature, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
For what reason is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the factors of enlightenment, the emptiness of the factors of enlightenment, the isolation of the factors of enlightenment, and the lack of intrinsic nature of the factors of enlightenment, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended.

Nor is the non-existence of the factors of enlightenment other than the emptiness of the factors of enlightenment, nor other than the isolation of the factors of enlightenment, nor other than the lack of intrinsic nature of the factors of enlightenment.
The Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit another, and the middle yet another—thus it is, venerable Śāradvatīputra.

For that which is the non-existence of the factors of awakening, that which is the emptiness of the factors of awakening, that which is the seclusion of the factors of awakening, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the factors of awakening;
and that which is the Bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the posterior limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the noble eightfold path does not exist, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;
because the noble eightfold path is empty, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;
because the noble eightfold path is secluded, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past.

Because the noble eightfold path lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because the noble eightfold path is non-existent, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; because the noble eightfold path is empty, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

Because the noble eightfold path is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit; because the noble eightfold path lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit; because the noble eightfold path is non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
Because of the emptiness of the noble eightfold path, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
because of the seclusion of the noble eightfold path, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
because of the lack of intrinsic nature of the noble eightfold path, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?
For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the noble eightfold path, within the emptiness of the noble eightfold path, within the seclusion of the noble eightfold path,

and within the lack of intrinsic nature of the noble eightfold path, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of the noble eightfold path one thing, the emptiness of the noble eightfold path another, and the seclusion of the noble eightfold path yet another.

"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the lack of intrinsic nature of the noble eightfold path is not one thing, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle yet another. For that which is the non-existence of the noble eightfold path, that which is the emptiness of the noble eightfold path,
that which is the solitude of the noble eightfold path, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the noble eightfold path, and that which is the bodhisattva— "
And that which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the noble truths do not exist, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
because the noble truths are empty, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
Because the noble truths are secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the past;

because the noble truths lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the past; because the noble truths do not exist, a bodhisattva [does not approach them] from the perspective of the future.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit by way of the emptiness of the noble truths;

a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit by way of the seclusion of the noble truths; a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the noble truths.
Because the noble truths do not exist, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
because the noble truths are empty, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
because the noble truths are secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the noble truths, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the noble truths, in the emptiness of the noble truths, in the solitude of the noble truths, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the noble truths, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the noble truths is not one thing, the emptiness of the noble truths another, the isolation of the noble truths another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the noble truths another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another,

the posterior limit another, and the middle another; for indeed, that which is the non-existence of the noble truths, that which is the emptiness of the noble truths, that which is the isolation of the noble truths, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the noble truths— [are all identical].
That which is a bodhisattva, that which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Because of the non-existence of meditative absorption (*dhyāna*), O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit;
because of the emptiness of meditative absorption, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit.

Because of the isolation of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāva*) of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the non-existence (*asattā*) of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.
A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the emptiness of meditative absorption; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the seclusion of meditative absorption;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the lack of intrinsic nature of meditative absorption.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the non-existence of meditative absorptions;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the emptiness of meditative absorptions;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the solitude of meditative absorptions.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?

For, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the meditative absorptions, within their emptiness, within their isolation, and within their lack of intrinsic nature, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of meditative absorption is not one thing, the emptiness of meditative absorption another, the solitude of meditative absorption another, the lack of intrinsic nature of meditative absorption another, and the bodhisattva another;

nor is the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another. For indeed, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of meditative absorption, that which is the emptiness of meditative absorption, that which is the solitude of meditative absorption, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of meditative absorption, and that which is the bodhisattva—[these are not distinct].
That which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the immeasurable, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
because of the emptiness of the immeasurable, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
Because they are devoid of measure, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of a prior limit;
because they lack the intrinsic nature of being measurable, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of a prior limit.
Due to the immeasurable non-existence of things, a bodhisattva does not approach a future limit;
due to the immeasurable emptiness of things, a bodhisattva does not approach a future limit;
due to the immeasurable solitude of things, a bodhisattva does not approach a future limit.
Because they lack the intrinsic nature of being immeasurable, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
because they lack the existence of being immeasurable, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
because they lack the emptiness of being immeasurable, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
Because the immeasurables are isolated, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of a middle;
because the immeasurables lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of a middle. Why is that?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the immeasurables, in the emptiness of the immeasurables, and in the isolation of the immeasurables...
In the absence of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), neither a prior limit is perceived, nor a subsequent limit is perceived, nor a middle is perceived.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the immeasurables is not one thing, the emptiness of the immeasurables another, the isolation of the immeasurables another, the absence of intrinsic nature in the immeasurables another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another; for that which is the non-existence of the immeasurables...

That which is the immeasurable emptiness, that which is the immeasurable seclusion, and that which is the immeasurable lack of intrinsic nature— the Bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the formless attainments, one does not apprehend a Bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the past by way of the emptiness of the formless attainments;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the past by way of the solitude of the formless attainments;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the past by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the formless attainments.

A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the non-existence of the formless attainments; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the emptiness of the formless attainments;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the solitude of the formless attainments.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the formless attainments, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the non-existence of the formless attainments, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the formless attainments, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
By virtue of the seclusion of the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
by virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the formless attainments, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?
Because, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the formless attainments, in the emptiness of the formless attainments, there is no formless attainment.

In the state of seclusion, in the lack of intrinsic nature of the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), neither a prior limit is perceived, nor a subsequent limit is perceived, nor a middle is perceived. Furthermore, the non-existence of the formless attainments is not other than the emptiness of the formless attainments;

the seclusion of the formless attainments is not other [than that]; the lack of intrinsic nature of the formless attainments is not other [than that]; the bodhisattva is not other [than that]; and the prior limit is not other [than that].
"Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the formless attainments,
the emptiness of the formless attainments, the solitude of the formless attainments,
and the lack of intrinsic nature of the formless attainments; and that which is the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the liberations, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

because of the emptiness of the liberations, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past. Because of the solitude of the liberations, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because of the lack of intrinsic nature of the liberations, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

Because of the non-existence of the liberations, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit; because of the emptiness of the liberations, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit; because of the solitude of the liberations, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit.
By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the liberations, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
by virtue of the non-existence (*asattā*) of the liberations, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
and by virtue of the emptiness (*śūnyatā*) of the liberations, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the seclusion of the liberations, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the liberations, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?
Because, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the liberations, in the emptiness of the liberations, and in the seclusion of the liberations—

In the absence of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the liberations (*vimokṣa*), neither a prior limit (*pūrvānta*) is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit (*aparānta*) is apprehended, nor a middle (*madhya*) is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the liberations is not one thing, the emptiness of the liberations another, the isolation of the liberations another, the absence of intrinsic nature of the liberations another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. Such is the case, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.

That which is the non-existence of the liberations, that which is the emptiness of the liberations, that which is the solitude of the liberations, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the liberations, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the serial attainments of meditative dwelling, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.
By virtue of the emptiness of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

by virtue of the seclusion of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

Because of the non-existence of the successive meditative attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; because of the emptiness of the successive meditative attainments, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; because of the isolation of the successive meditative attainments, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit.

By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
by virtue of the non-existence (*asattā*) of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
and by virtue of the emptiness (*śūnyatā*) of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
By virtue of the seclusion of the attainments of the successive dwellings, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of the attainments of the successive dwellings, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the attainments of the successive dwellings and in the emptiness of the attainments of the successive dwellings...

In the seclusion of the attainments of the successive dwellings, in the lack of intrinsic nature of the attainments of the successive dwellings, neither a prior limit is perceived, nor a subsequent limit is perceived, nor a middle is perceived. Furthermore, the non-existence of the attainments of the successive dwellings is not other than the emptiness of the attainments of the successive dwellings, the seclusion of the attainments of the successive dwellings, or the lack of intrinsic nature of the attainments of the successive dwellings.
"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit is another, and the posterior limit is another.

For that which is the non-existence of the serial attainments of meditative absorption, that which is the emptiness of the serial attainments of meditative absorption, that which is the solitude of the serial attainments of meditative absorption,

and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the serial attainments of meditative absorption— these are distinct from that which is the Bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, and that which is the posterior limit."
And that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
because of the emptiness of the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
Because the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the past;
because the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are devoid of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the past;
because the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future.
By way of the emptiness of the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the seclusion of the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
Because of the non-existence of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
because of the emptiness of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
because of the seclusion of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle.

By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the gateways to liberation—emptiness (*śūnyatā*), signlessness (*animitta*), and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*)—the bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; in the emptiness of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; in the isolation of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—[there is no such approach].

The prior limit is not apprehended, the subsequent limit is not apprehended, and the middle is not apprehended. Furthermore, the non-existence of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not other than the emptiness of those gateways to liberation; their isolation is not other than them; their lack of intrinsic nature is not other than them; and the Bodhisattva is not other [than these], nor is the prior limit other.

"Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the future limit, the other [the past], and the middle—namely, the non-existence of the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;

the emptiness of the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; the seclusion of the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; the lack of intrinsic nature of the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; as well as the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the existence of the superknowledges, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by way of the emptiness of the superknowledges, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by way of the isolation of the superknowledges, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By way of the intrinsic nature of the superknowledges, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past; by way of the existence of the superknowledges, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future; by way of the emptiness of the superknowledges, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.

Because the superknowledges are isolated, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit; because the superknowledges have the nature of being such, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit; because the superknowledges lack substantial existence, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the emptiness of the superknowledges;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the seclusion of the superknowledges;
a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the intrinsic nature of the superknowledges. Why is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of the superknowledges (*abhijñā*), within the emptiness of the superknowledges, within the solitude of the superknowledges, and within the intrinsic nature of the superknowledges, neither a prior limit is perceived, nor a subsequent limit is perceived, nor a middle is perceived.

Nor is the existence of the superknowledges other than the emptiness of the superknowledges, nor the solitude of the superknowledges, nor the intrinsic nature of the superknowledges other than the Bodhisattva.
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, for the prior limit is one thing, the posterior limit is another, and the middle is yet another; however, that which is the existence of the superknowledges,

that which is the emptiness of the superknowledges, that which is the solitude of the superknowledges, and that which is the intrinsic nature of the superknowledges— along with the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

by way of the emptiness of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the solitude of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of meditative concentration, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by virtue of the non-existence of meditative concentration, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future; and by virtue of the emptiness of meditative concentration, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
Because of the solitude of samādhi, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because of the lack of intrinsic nature of samādhi, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because of the non-existence of samādhi, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
by way of the solitude of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of meditative concentration, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of concentration, the emptiness of concentration, the solitude of concentration, and the lack of intrinsic nature of concentration, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of concentration one thing, the emptiness of concentration another, the solitude of concentration another, the lack of intrinsic nature of concentration another, and [the Tathāgata] another.

"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit still another. For indeed, that which is the non-existence of samādhi, that which is the emptiness of samādhi, that which is the solitude of samādhi, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of samādhi, and that which is the bodhisattva, and that which is the prior limit— "
That which is the future limit and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the gateways of dhāraṇī do not exist, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit;
because the gateways of dhāraṇī are empty, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit.
Because the gateways of dhāraṇī are secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past;

because the gateways of dhāraṇī lack intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past; because the gateways of dhāraṇī are non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future.
By means of the emptiness of the gateways of dhāraṇī, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit;

by means of the solitude of the gateways of dhāraṇī, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by means of the lack of intrinsic nature of the gateways of dhāraṇī, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit.
By way of the non-existence of the gateways of dhāraṇī, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the gateways of dhāraṇī, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of the gateways of dhāraṇī, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the gateways of mnemonic formulas, within their emptiness, within their isolation, and within their lack of intrinsic nature, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the gateways of dhāraṇī is not one thing, the emptiness of the gateways of dhāraṇī another, the solitude of the gateways of dhāraṇī another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the gateways of dhāraṇī another,
the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another. For indeed, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra,
that which is the non-existence of the gateways of dhāraṇī, that which is the emptiness of the gateways of dhāraṇī, and that which is the solitude of the gateways of dhāraṇī— [are all one].
And the intrinsic nature of the gateways of dhāraṇīs, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—
all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the powers of a Tathāgata do not exist, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;

by way of the isolation of the powers of a Tathāgata, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the powers of a Tathāgata, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past.

A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the non-existence of the powers of a Tathāgata; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the isolation of the powers of a Tathāgata.

By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the powers of a Tathāgata, a bodhisattva does not approach [them] from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the non-existence of the powers of a Tathāgata, a bodhisattva does not approach [them] from the perspective of the middle; by way of the emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata, a bodhisattva does not approach [them] from the perspective of the middle.
By virtue of the isolation of the powers of a Tathāgata, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
by virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of the powers of a Tathāgata, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that? Because, O Venerable One, [they do not exist].
Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the powers of a Tathāgata, the emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata, the solitude of the powers of a Tathāgata,

and the lack of intrinsic nature of the powers of a Tathāgata, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, the non-existence of the powers of a Tathāgata is not one thing, the emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata another, and the solitude of the powers of a Tathāgata yet another.

The nature of the powers of a Tathāgata is not one thing, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle yet another. For, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the powers of a Tathāgata,

that which is the emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata, that which is the solitude of the powers of a Tathāgata, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the powers of a Tathāgata, and that which is the Bodhisattva— [all these are identical].
And that which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the fearlessnesses, a bodhisattva does not approach [them] from the past limit;
because of the emptiness of the fearlessnesses, a bodhisattva does not approach [them] from the past limit.

Because of the isolation of fearlessness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the lack of intrinsic nature of fearlessness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the non-existence of fearlessness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.
By way of the emptiness of the fearlessnesses, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit;

by way of the isolation of the fearlessnesses, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the fearlessnesses, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the non-existence of the fearlessnesses, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the fearlessnesses, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
by way of the seclusion of the fearlessnesses, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the fearlessnesses, within the emptiness of the fearlessnesses, within the isolation of the fearlessnesses, and within the lack of intrinsic nature of the fearlessnesses, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the fearlessnesses is not one thing, the emptiness of the fearlessnesses another, the seclusion of the fearlessnesses another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the fearlessnesses another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. For indeed, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the fearlessnesses, that which is the emptiness of the fearlessnesses, that which is the seclusion of the fearlessnesses, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the fearlessnesses— [these are all identical].
That which is a bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the subsequent limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit;
because of the emptiness of the analytical knowledges, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.

Because the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the past; because the analytical knowledges lack intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the past; because the analytical knowledges do not exist, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future.

By way of the emptiness of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the seclusion of the analytical knowledges, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the analytical knowledges, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the non-existence of the analytical knowledges, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the analytical knowledges, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
Because of the isolation of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle;
because of the lack of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the analytical knowledges, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the middle. For what reason?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the analytical knowledges, in the emptiness of the analytical knowledges, and in the isolation of the analytical knowledges...
In the absence of intrinsic nature (*svabhāvatā*) of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), neither a prior limit is perceived, nor a subsequent limit is perceived, nor a middle is perceived.
