Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the analytical knowledges is not one thing, their emptiness another, their solitude another, their absence of intrinsic nature another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. Thus it is, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.

The non-existence of the analytical knowledges, the emptiness of the analytical knowledges, the solitude of the analytical knowledges, and the lack of intrinsic nature of the analytical knowledges— the Bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—
all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the existence of great compassion, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

by virtue of the emptiness of great compassion, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by virtue of the solitude of great compassion, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By virtue of the intrinsic nature of great compassion, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by virtue of the non-existence of great compassion, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future; and by virtue of the emptiness of great compassion, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
Because great compassion is empty, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because great compassion has the nature of emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because great compassion is non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
A bodhisattva does not approach a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle way by way of the emptiness of great compassion,
nor does he approach a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle way by way of the seclusion of great compassion,
nor does he approach a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle way by way of the intrinsic nature of great compassion. Why is that?

For indeed, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of great compassion, the emptiness of great compassion, the solitude of great compassion, and the intrinsic nature of great compassion, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended. Nor is the existence of great compassion one thing, the emptiness of great compassion another, the solitude of great compassion another, the intrinsic nature of great compassion another, or [the Tathāgata] another.
The Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit another, and the middle yet another—thus it is, venerable Śāradvatīputra.

For that which is the existence of great compassion, that which is the emptiness of great compassion, that which is the solitude of great compassion, and that which is the intrinsic nature of great compassion;
and that which is the Bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the posterior limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the unique attributes of a Buddha do not exist, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit. Because the unique attributes of a Buddha are empty, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.
Because the unique attributes of a Buddha are secluded, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.
Because the unique attributes of a Buddha lack intrinsic nature, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.

Due to the non-existence of the unique attributes of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; due to the emptiness of the unique attributes of a Buddha, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; due to the solitude of the unique attributes of a Buddha, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit;
by way of the non-existence (*asattā*) of the unique qualities of a Buddha, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
and by way of the emptiness (*śūnyatā*) of the unique qualities of a Buddha, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
Because the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle;
because the unique qualities of a Buddha lack intrinsic nature (*asvabhāva*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle. Why is that?
Because, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the unique qualities of a Buddha and in the emptiness of the unique qualities of a Buddha...

In the seclusion of the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) and in the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the unique qualities of a Buddha, neither a prior limit (*pūrvānta*) is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit (*aparānta*) is apprehended, nor a middle (*madhya*) is apprehended. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the unique qualities of a Buddha is not one thing, their emptiness another, their seclusion another, and their lack of intrinsic nature another;
nor is the bodhisattva one thing, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. Thus it is, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.
That which is the non-existence of the unique qualities of a Buddha, that which is the emptiness of the unique qualities of a Buddha, that which is the solitude of the unique qualities of a Buddha,

and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the unique qualities of a Buddha— along with the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the dharma-realm is non-existent, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because the dharma-realm is empty, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because the dharma-realm is secluded, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
Because the *dharmadhātu* has no intrinsic nature, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past limit;
because the *dharmadhātu* does not exist, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit;
because the *dharmadhātu* is empty, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit.
Because the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because the realm of phenomena lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because the realm of phenomena is non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of the dharma-realm, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the solitude of the dharma-realm, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?

For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the dharma-realm, in the emptiness of the dharma-realm, in the solitude of the dharma-realm, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of the dharma-realm one thing, and the emptiness of the dharma-realm another, and the solitude of the dharma-realm another, and the lack of intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm another.
The Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the posterior limit another, and the middle yet another; for, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the dharma-realm,
that which is the emptiness of the dharma-realm, that which is the solitude of the dharma-realm, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm— [all these are distinct].
The bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of suchness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the prior limit;
because of the emptiness of suchness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the prior limit.
By virtue of the solitude of suchness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;

by virtue of the intrinsic nature of suchness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; and by virtue of the non-existence of suchness, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the emptiness of suchness;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the seclusion of suchness;
a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the intrinsic nature of suchness.
By way of the existence of suchness, one does not approach a bodhisattva from the middle; by way of the emptiness of suchness, one does not approach a bodhisattva from the middle;
by way of the solitude of suchness, one does not approach a bodhisattva from the middle.
By virtue of having suchness as its intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of suchness, within the emptiness of suchness, within the solitude of suchness, and within the intrinsic nature of suchness, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of suchness is not one thing, the emptiness of suchness another, the seclusion of suchness another, the intrinsic nature of suchness another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another; for indeed,
that which is the existence of suchness, that which is the emptiness of suchness, that which is the seclusion of suchness, and that which is the intrinsic nature of suchness— [are all one].
That which is the bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the posterior limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the prior limit;
because of the emptiness of the limit of reality, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the prior limit.
Because the limit of reality is secluded, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because the limit of reality lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
because the limit of reality is non-existent, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

By way of the emptiness of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the isolation of the limit of reality, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the limit of reality, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit.
Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
because the limit of reality is empty, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle;
because the limit of reality is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle.
Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) lacks intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. For what reason?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the limit of reality, in the emptiness of the limit of reality, in the solitude of the limit of reality, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the limit of reality...

The prior limit is not apprehended, the posterior limit is not apprehended, and the middle is not apprehended. Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭyasattā*) is not other than the emptiness of the limit of reality, nor other than the isolation of the limit of reality, nor other than the lack of intrinsic nature of the limit of reality; and the Bodhisattva is not other [than these], nor is the prior limit other, nor the posterior limit other, nor the middle other—because that which is the non-existence of the limit of reality is [identical to them].
That which is the emptiness of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), that which is the solitude of the limit of reality, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the limit of reality—

the Bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible. Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, due to the non-existence of the inconceivable realm, a Bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of the inconceivable realm, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by way of the solitude of the inconceivable realm, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the inconceivable realm, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.
Because the inconceivable realm is non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because the inconceivable realm is empty, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because the inconceivable realm is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit.
Because the inconceivable realm has the nature of non-self-nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because the inconceivable realm is non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle;
because the inconceivable realm is empty, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
Because the inconceivable realm is secluded, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle;
because the inconceivable realm lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. Why is that?
For, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the inconceivable realm, within the emptiness of the inconceivable realm, and within the seclusion of the inconceivable realm—
In the nature of the inconceivable realm, a prior limit is not apprehended, a subsequent limit is not apprehended, and a middle is not apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the existence of the inconceivable realm is not one thing, its emptiness another, its solitude another, its nature of being the inconceivable realm another, and the bodhisattva another; nor is the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another. Thus it is, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.

That which is the non-existence of the inconceivable realm, that which is the emptiness of the inconceivable realm, that which is the solitude of the inconceivable realm, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the inconceivable realm, and that which is the bodhisattva, and that which is the prior limit, and that which is the subsequent limit, and that which is the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of a śrāvaka, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;

by way of the emptiness of a śrāvaka, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the isolation of a śrāvaka, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past.

A bodhisattva does not approach from the past by way of the intrinsic nature of a śrāvaka; a bodhisattva does not approach from the future by way of the non-existence of a śrāvaka; a bodhisattva does not approach from the future by way of the emptiness of a śrāvaka.
A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit through the isolation of the śrāvaka,
nor does a bodhisattva approach the future limit through the lack of intrinsic nature of the śrāvaka.
By way of the non-existence of the śrāvaka, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of the śrāvaka, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle; by way of the seclusion of the śrāvaka, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.
By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of a śrāvaka, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?

For, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of a śrāvaka, in the emptiness of a śrāvaka, in the isolation of a śrāvaka, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of a śrāvaka, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of a śrāvaka is not one thing, the emptiness of a śrāvaka another, the solitude of a śrāvaka another, the lack of intrinsic nature of a śrāvaka another,

the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. For indeed, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of a śrāvaka, that which is the emptiness of a śrāvaka, that which is the solitude of a śrāvaka, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of a śrāvaka— [are all identical].
That which is the bodhisattva, that which is the past limit, that which is the future limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, due to the non-existence of the pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit;
due to the emptiness of the pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit.
Because of the solitude of the pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past;

because of the lack of intrinsic nature of the pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; because of the non-existence of the pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
By way of the emptiness of the pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit;

by way of the solitude of the pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit.
By way of the non-existence of a pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the middle;
by way of the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the middle; by way of the isolation of a pratyekabuddha, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the middle.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of a pratyekabuddha. Why is that?

For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of a pratyekabuddha, in the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha, in the isolation of a pratyekabuddha, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of a pratyekabuddha, neither a prior limit nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor is a middle apprehended.

It is perceived. Furthermore, the non-existence of a pratyekabuddha is not one thing, the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha another, the seclusion of a pratyekabuddha another, the lack of intrinsic nature of a pratyekabuddha another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another. For, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of a pratyekabuddha and that which is the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha—[are they different? It is perceived [that they are not]. For, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of a pratyekabuddha and that which is the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha—[are they different? It is perceived [that they are not]. For, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of a pratyekabuddha and that which is the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha—[are they different? It is perceived [that they are not]. For, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of a pratyekabuddha and that which is the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha—[are they different? It is perceived [that they are not]. Furthermore, the non-existence of a pratyekabuddha is not one thing, the emptiness of a pratyekabuddha another, the seclusion of a pratyekabuddha another, the lack of intrinsic nature of a pratyekabuddha another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit

The solitude of a pratyekabuddha, the lack of intrinsic nature of a pratyekabuddha, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle— all this is non-dual and indivisible. Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of a bodhisattva, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the prior limit.
By way of the emptiness of a bodhisattva, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past;

by way of the solitude of a bodhisattva, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

By way of the non-existence of a bodhisattva, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the emptiness of a bodhisattva, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the solitude of a bodhisattva, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit.

By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the non-existence of a bodhisattva, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle; by way of the emptiness of a bodhisattva, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the isolation of the bodhisattva, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the bodhisattva, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the middle. Why is that?
Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the bodhisattva, in the emptiness of the bodhisattva, and in the isolation of the bodhisattva...
In the absence of intrinsic nature in a bodhisattva, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of a bodhisattva is not one thing, the emptiness of a bodhisattva another, the isolation of a bodhisattva another, the absence of intrinsic nature in a bodhisattva another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another. Thus it is, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra.
That which is the non-existence of a bodhisattva, that which is the emptiness of a bodhisattva, that which is the isolation of a bodhisattva,
that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva, and that which is the bodhisattva himself— along with the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—
all this is non-dual and indivisible.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of the omniscient one, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit;
by way of the emptiness of the omniscient one, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit;
by way of the isolation of the omniscient one, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit.

By way of the intrinsic nature of omniscience, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the past; by way of the non-existence of omniscience, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future; and by way of the emptiness of omniscience, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the perspective of the future.
Because omniscience is empty, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because omniscience lacks intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit;
because omniscience is non-existent, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.
By way of the emptiness of omniscience, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the isolation of omniscience, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle;
by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of omniscience, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that?
For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of an omniscient one, the emptiness of an omniscient one, the solitude of an omniscient one,

and the lack of intrinsic nature of an omniscient one, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of an omniscient one other [than these], nor is the emptiness of an omniscient one other, nor is the solitude of an omniscient one other, nor is the lack of intrinsic nature of an omniscient one other.

"O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the Bodhisattva is one thing, the prior limit another, and the subsequent limit another, and the middle yet another; for that which is the non-existence of the omniscient one, that which is the emptiness of the omniscient one, that which is the solitude of the omniscient one,
and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the omniscient one— [all these] and the Bodhisattva, and the prior limit, and the subsequent limit, and [the middle]..."
All this middle is non-dual and indivisible.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit,
nor is a bodhisattva apprehended from the perspective of the future limit.
A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.

Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, as to why you say, "For what reason should the boundlessness of a bodhisattva be understood through the boundlessness of form?"—Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form is equal to space. Why is that?

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is just as, for example, no beginning of space is apprehended, no end of space is apprehended, and no middle of space is apprehended. Because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space. In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of form is apprehended, no end of form is apprehended, and no middle of form is apprehended.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of specific characteristics is equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;
because it is infinite and boundless,
it is conventionally designated by the name "space."
In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended,
and no middle is apprehended.

Based on the emptiness of the emptiness of specific characteristics, neither the end nor the middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the emptiness of specific characteristics, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
As for what you have said:
For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattva be understood through the boundlessness of the emptiness of non-apprehension?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of non-apprehension is equal to space. Why is that?
It is because, for example, no prior limit of space is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended.
Because it is infinite and boundless, space is conventionally designated by the name "space.
In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the emptiness of non-apprehension, no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended,
by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of non-apprehension.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the emptiness of non-apprehension, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
As for what you asked: "For what reason is the boundlessness of the bodhisattva to be understood through the boundlessness of the emptiness of non-existence?"
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of non-existence is equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;
because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space."

In the same way, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), no beginning is apprehended, no end is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended, by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of non-existence;

nor is an end or a middle of emptiness itself apprehended. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the emptiness of non-existence, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
Furthermore, as to what you have said:
"For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattva be understood through the boundlessness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;
because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"—

in the very same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of intrinsic-nature emptiness is perceived, no end of intrinsic-nature emptiness is perceived, and no middle of intrinsic-nature emptiness is perceived, [due to its] emptiness of intrinsic-nature emptiness.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
As for what you have asked:
"For what reason is it that through the boundlessness of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence [the bodhisattva is boundless]?"
It should be understood that the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is such, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is equal to space. For what reason?
Just as, for example, no prior limit of space is perceived, no subsequent limit is perceived, and no middle is perceived; [so it is with the bodhisattva].
Because it is infinite and boundless, space is conventionally designated by the name "space.
In the same way, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, no prior limit is perceived, no subsequent limit is perceived, and no middle is perceived;
this is on account of the emptiness of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
As for what you asked:
"For what reason is the boundlessness of the bodhisattva to be understood through the boundlessness of the applications of mindfulness? [it is as follows:]
The applications of mindfulness, venerable Śāradvatīputra, are equal to space. Why is that?
It is because, just as no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;
it is by virtue of being infinite and boundless that space is conventionally designated by the name "space."
In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the applications of mindfulness is apprehended, no end is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended;

nor is an end or a middle apprehended within the emptiness of the applications of mindfulness. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the applications of mindfulness, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
As for what you have said:
For what reason should it be understood that the boundlessness of the *samyakprahāṇas* constitutes the boundlessness of the bodhisattvas?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the *samyakprahāṇas* are equal to space. Why is that?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is because, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived.
Because it is infinite and boundless, space is conventionally designated by the name "space.

In the same way, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, no prior limit of the right efforts is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended; for the emptiness of the right efforts, neither a limit nor a middle is apprehended. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the right efforts, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
Furthermore, as for what you have said:
"For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of the bases of miraculous power?
O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the bases of miraculous power are equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;
because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"—
even so, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is it with the bases of psychic power.
Neither a beginning is perceived, nor an end is perceived, nor a middle is perceived, by reason of the emptiness of the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*);

and within emptiness, neither an end nor a middle is perceived. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the bases of psychic power, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva should be understood.
Furthermore, as for what you have said:
"For what reason should the infinity of bodhisattvas be understood through the infinity of the faculties?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the faculties are equal to space. For what reason?
Just as, for example, no beginning of space is apprehended, no end of space is apprehended, and no middle of space is apprehended;
because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"—
even so, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the faculties is apprehended, no end of the faculties is apprehended, and no middle of the faculties is apprehended.

Based on the emptiness of the faculties, neither the end nor the middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should understand that because the faculties are limitless, the bodhisattva is likewise limitless.
As for what you have further said:
For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of the powers?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the powers are equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no prior limit of space is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended; [so it is with the powers].
Because it is infinite and boundless, space is conventionally designated by the name "space.

In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the powers is apprehended, no end of the powers is apprehended, and no middle of the powers is apprehended, by virtue of the emptiness of the powers.
Nor is an end or a middle of emptiness itself apprehended. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should understand that because the powers are limitless, the bodhisattva is also limitless.
Furthermore, as for what you said:

"For what reason should the infinity of bodhisattvas be understood through the infinity of the factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga)?"—Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the factors of enlightenment are equal to space. For what reason?

Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived; and because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"— even so, venerable Śāradvatīputra, due to the emptiness of the factors of enlightenment, no beginning of the factors of enlightenment is perceived, no end of the factors of enlightenment is perceived, and no middle of the factors of enlightenment is perceived.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, through the boundlessness of the factors of enlightenment, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood. As for what you asked: "For what reason is the boundlessness of the bodhisattva to be understood through the boundlessness of the noble eightfold path? [it is as follows:]
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the noble eightfold path is equal to space. Why is that?
It is because, just as in the case of space, no beginning is perceived, no end is perceived, and no middle is perceived.
Because it is infinite and boundless, space is conventionally designated by the name "space";
in the very same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no prior limit of the noble eightfold path is apprehended, nor is a subsequent limit apprehended.
A middle is not apprehended, by virtue of the emptiness of the noble eightfold path;

nor is an end or a middle apprehended within emptiness itself. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should understand that because the noble eightfold path is limitless, the bodhisattva is likewise limitless.
Furthermore, as for what you said:
"For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of the noble truths?"—Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the noble truths are equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;
and because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"—
even so, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the noble truths is perceived, no end of the noble truths is perceived, and no middle of the noble truths is perceived.

Based on the emptiness of the noble truths, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the boundlessness of the noble truths, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
As for what you have said:
For what reason should the boundlessness of bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*)?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the meditative absorptions are equal to space. Why is that?
It is because, for example, no prior limit of space is perceived, no subsequent limit is perceived, and no middle is perceived.
Because it is infinite and boundless, space is conventionally designated by the name "space.
In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, due to the emptiness of meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*), no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended;

nor is an end or a middle apprehended within emptiness itself. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the meditative absorptions, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
Furthermore, as for what you have said:
"For what reason should the boundlessness of bodhisattvas be understood through the immeasurability and boundlessness [of phenomena]?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the immeasurables are equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;
because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"—
in the very same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the immeasurables is perceived, no end of the immeasurables is perceived, and no middle of the immeasurables is perceived.

Based on the immeasurable emptiness, neither the end nor the middle of emptiness is apprehended. In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, through its immeasurability and boundlessness, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva should be understood.
As for what you have further said:
For what reason should the boundlessness of bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of the formless attainments?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the formless attainments are equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no prior limit of space is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended; [so it is with the formless attainments].
Because it is infinite and boundless, space is conventionally designated by the name "space.
In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no prior limit of the formless attainments is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended,
by virtue of the emptiness of the formless attainments.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should understand that because the formless attainments are limitless, the bodhisattva is likewise limitless.
As for what you asked: "For what reason should the bodhisattva be understood as limitless because the eight liberations are limitless?"
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the eight liberations are equal to space. Why is that?
It is because, for example, no prior limit of space is perceived, no subsequent limit is perceived, and no middle is perceived;
it is by virtue of being infinite and boundless that it is conventionally designated as 'space'."
In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the liberations is apprehended, no end is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended, by reason of the emptiness of the liberations;

nor is an end or a middle of emptiness itself apprehended. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should understand that because the liberations are limitless, the bodhisattvas are also limitless.
Furthermore, as for what you have said:
"For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of the successive attainments of the meditative dwellings?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the successive attainments of the meditative dwellings are equal to space. Why is that?

Just as, for example, no beginning of space is apprehended, no end of space is apprehended, and no middle of space is apprehended; and because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"— even so, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, of these successive dwellings and meditative attainments, no beginning is apprehended, no end is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended.

Based on the emptiness of the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by this method, because the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings are limitless, the bodhisattva is likewise limitless.
As for what you have further said:
For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattva be understood through the boundlessness of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are equal to space. Why is that?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is because, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived.
Because it is infinite and boundless, space is conventionally designated by the name "space.

In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, regarding the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—no prior limit is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended, due to the emptiness of the gateways to liberation: emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is established.
As for what you asked:
"For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattva be understood through the boundlessness of the superknowledges? [the answer is as follows:]
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the superknowledges are equal to space. Why is that?
It is because, just as no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;
it is by virtue of being infinite and boundless that "space" is conventionally designated.

In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of supernormal knowledge (*abhijñā*) is apprehended, no end is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended, by reason of the emptiness of supernormal knowledge.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, it should be understood that because supernormal knowledge is limitless, the bodhisattva is also limitless.
Furthermore, as for what you have said:
"For what reason should the boundlessness of bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of meditative concentrations?
O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, meditative concentrations are equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;

and because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"— even so, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, due to the emptiness of meditative concentrations (*samādhi-śūnyatā*), no beginning of these concentrations is perceived, no end is perceived, and no middle is perceived.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood through the boundlessness of meditative concentration.
As for what you asked:
"For what reason is the boundlessness of the bodhisattva to be understood through the boundlessness of the gateways of dhāraṇī?"
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the gateways of dhāraṇīs are equal to space. Why is that?
It is because, just as in the case of space, no beginning is perceived, no end is perceived, and no middle is perceived;
it is by virtue of being infinite and boundless that it is conventionally designated by the name "space."

In the same way, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the gateways of dhāraṇī is apprehended, no end is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended, by reason of the emptiness of the gateways of dhāraṇī;

nor is an end or a middle apprehended within emptiness itself. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should understand that because the gateways of dhāraṇī are limitless, the bodhisattvas are likewise limitless.
As for what you have further said:
For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of the powers of a Tathāgata?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the powers of a Tathāgata are equal to space. Why is that?

Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived; and because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"— even so, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the powers of a Tathāgata is perceived, no end of the powers of a Tathāgata is perceived, and no middle of the powers of a Tathāgata is perceived, due to the emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should understand the boundlessness of the bodhisattva through the boundlessness of the powers of a Tathāgata.
As for what you have said:
"For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattva be understood through the boundlessness of the fearlessnesses?"
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the grounds of self-confidence are equal to space. For what reason?
Just as, for example, no prior limit of space is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended;
because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name 'space.'"

In the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya) is apprehended, no end is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended, by reason of the emptiness of the fearlessnesses;

nor is an end or a middle apprehended in emptiness itself. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the fearlessnesses, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood.
As for what you have said:
For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*)?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the analytical knowledges are equal to space. Why is that?
It is just as, for example, no prior limit of space is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended.
Because it is infinite and boundless, space is conventionally designated as "space.

In the same way, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) is apprehended, no end is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended, by virtue of the emptiness of the analytical knowledges;

nor is an end or a middle apprehended within emptiness itself. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, through the boundlessness of the analytical knowledges, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva should be understood.
Furthermore, as for what you have said:
"For what reason should the boundlessness of the bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of great compassion?"—Venerable Śāradvatīputra, great compassion is equal to space. Why is that?
Just as, for example, no beginning of space is perceived, no end of space is perceived, and no middle of space is perceived;
and because it is infinite and boundless, it is conventionally designated by the name "space"—

in the same way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, no beginning of great compassion is perceived, no end of great compassion is perceived, and no middle of great compassion is perceived, on account of the emptiness of great compassion.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should understand that because great compassion is limitless, the bodhisattva is likewise limitless.
As for what you have said:
For what reason should the boundlessness of bodhisattvas be understood through the boundlessness of the unique qualities of a buddha?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the unique qualities of a buddha are equal to space. Why is that?
It is just as, for example, no prior limit of space is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended.
Just as space is conventionally designated by the name "space" because it is infinite and boundless,
even so, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, no prior limit of the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended,
by virtue of the emptiness of the unique qualities of a Buddha.

Furthermore, neither an end nor a middle of emptiness is apprehended. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should understand that because the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are limitless, the bodhisattva is likewise limitless.
As for what you said, Venerable Śāradvatīputra: "For what reason is it that even such a thing as 'form is a bodhisattva' does not exist and is not apprehended?"
For what reason is it that even "feeling is a bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended;
even "perception is a bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended;
and even "formative factors are a bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended?
"Consciousness is a bodhisattva"—even this is not found and is not apprehended. "Form, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is empty of form. Why is that?
Because in emptiness, neither form nor a bodhisattva is found.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, 'form is a bodhisattva'—even this is not found and is not apprehended. Feeling is empty of feeling. Why is that?"

For in emptiness, form is not found, nor is a bodhisattva. In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, feeling as a bodhisattva is likewise neither found nor apprehended. Perception is empty of perception. Why is that?
For in emptiness, perception is not found, nor is a bodhisattva.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, even the designation "bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended. Formations are empty of formations. Why is that?
Because within emptiness, neither formations nor a bodhisattva exist.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, even "formations are a bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended. Consciousness is empty of consciousness. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither consciousness nor a bodhisattva exists.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, even "consciousness is a bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of generosity is empty of the perfection of generosity. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the perfection of generosity does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The perfection of ethical discipline is empty of the perfection of ethical discipline. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the perfection of ethical discipline does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The perfection of patience is empty of the perfection of patience. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the perfection of patience does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The perfection of vigor is empty of the perfection of vigor. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the perfection of vigor does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The perfection of meditation is empty of the perfection of meditation. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the perfection of meditation does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The perfection of wisdom is empty of the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the perfection of wisdom does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, internal emptiness is empty of internal emptiness. Why is that?
Because within emptiness, neither internal emptiness nor a bodhisattva is found.
External emptiness is empty of external emptiness. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither external emptiness nor a bodhisattva exists;
internal-external emptiness is empty of internal-external emptiness. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither internal-external emptiness nor a bodhisattva exists.
The emptiness of emptiness is empty of the emptiness of emptiness. Why is that?
Because within emptiness, neither the emptiness of emptiness nor a bodhisattva exists.
Great emptiness is empty of great emptiness. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither great emptiness nor a bodhisattva exists;
ultimate emptiness is empty of ultimate emptiness. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither ultimate emptiness nor a bodhisattva exists.
The emptiness of the conditioned is empty of the emptiness of the conditioned. For what reason?
Because within emptiness, neither the emptiness of the conditioned nor a bodhisattva is found.
The emptiness of the unconditioned is empty of the emptiness of the unconditioned. For what reason?
For within emptiness, the emptiness of the unconditioned is not found, nor is the bodhisattva;
it is empty by virtue of the emptiness of the ultimate. Why is that?
For within emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate is not found, nor is the bodhisattva.
The emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is empty by virtue of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end. For what reason?
Because within emptiness, neither the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end nor a bodhisattva exists.
The emptiness of non-dispersal is empty by virtue of the emptiness of non-dispersal. For what reason?
For within emptiness, non-dispersive emptiness is not found, nor is a bodhisattva;
intrinsic emptiness is empty of intrinsic emptiness. Why is that?
For within emptiness, intrinsic emptiness is not found, nor is a bodhisattva.
The emptiness of all dharmas is empty of the emptiness of all dharmas. For what reason?
Because within emptiness, neither the emptiness of all dharmas nor a bodhisattva exists.
The emptiness of specific characteristics is empty of the emptiness of specific characteristics. Why is that?
Because within emptiness, neither the emptiness of specific characteristics nor the bodhisattva exists;
the emptiness of non-apprehension is empty of the emptiness of non-apprehension. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither the emptiness of non-apprehension nor the bodhisattva exists;
it is empty by virtue of the emptiness of non-existence and the emptiness of existence. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither the emptiness of non-existence nor the bodhisattva exists.
The emptiness of existence is empty of the emptiness of existence. Why is that?
Because within emptiness, neither the emptiness of existence nor the bodhisattva exists.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither the emptiness of the nature of non-existence nor the bodhisattva exists.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, the applications of mindfulness are empty of the applications of mindfulness. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither the applications of mindfulness nor the bodhisattva exist. The right efforts are empty of the right efforts. Why is that?
For within emptiness, the right efforts do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The bases of psychic power are empty of the bases of psychic power. Why is that?
For within emptiness, the right efforts do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The faculties are empty of the faculties. Why is that?
For within emptiness, the faculties do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The powers are empty of the powers. Why is that?
For within emptiness, the powers do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The factors of enlightenment are empty of the factors of enlightenment. Why is that?
For within emptiness, the factors of enlightenment do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The noble eightfold path is empty of the noble eightfold path. Why is that?
For within emptiness, the noble eightfold path does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The noble truths are empty of the noble truths. Why is that?
For within emptiness the noble truths do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The meditative absorptions are empty of meditative absorptions. Why is that?

For within emptiness the meditative absorptions do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The immeasurables are empty of immeasurables. Why is that? For within emptiness the immeasurables do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The formless attainments are empty of formless attainments. Why is that?

For in emptiness, the formless attainments do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The eight liberations are empty of the eight liberations. Why is that? Because in emptiness, the eight liberations do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The nine successive meditative attainments are empty of the nine successive meditative attainments. Why is that?
Because in emptiness, the nine successive meditative attainments do not exist, nor does [the bodhisattva].

The Bodhisattva: the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are empty of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Why is that? Because within emptiness, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—do not exist, nor does the Bodhisattva. The superknowledges are empty of superknowledges. Why is that? Because within emptiness, the superknowledges do not exist, nor does the Bodhisattva. The meditative concentrations are empty of meditative concentrations. Why is that?
For within emptiness, the meditative concentrations do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The gateways of dhāraṇī are empty of the gateways of dhāraṇī. Why is that?
Because within emptiness, the gateways of dhāraṇī do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The powers of a Tathāgata are empty of the powers of a Tathāgata. Why is that?
Because within emptiness, the powers of a Tathāgata do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The grounds of self-confidence are empty of the grounds of self-confidence. Why is that?

For indeed, the grounds of self-confidence do not exist within emptiness, nor does the bodhisattva. The analytical knowledges are empty of analytical knowledges. Why is that? For indeed, the analytical knowledges do not exist within emptiness, nor does the bodhisattva. Great compassion is empty of great compassion. Why is that?
For indeed, great compassion does not exist within emptiness, nor does the bodhisattva. The unique qualities of a buddha are empty of the unique qualities of a buddha. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the unique qualities of a Buddha do not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is empty of the realm of phenomena. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the realm of phenomena does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. Suchness (*tathatā*) is empty of suchness. Why is that?
For in emptiness, suchness does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is empty of the limit of reality. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) nor a bodhisattva exists. The inconceivable realm is empty of the inconceivable realm. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither the inconceivable realm nor a bodhisattva exists. Omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is empty of omniscience. Why is that?
For within emptiness, neither omniscience nor a bodhisattva exists. The knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) is empty of the knowledge of the aspects of the path. Why is that?

For in emptiness, the knowledge of the aspects of the path does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The knowledge of all aspects is empty of the knowledge of all aspects. Why is that? For in emptiness, the knowledge of all aspects does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The vehicle of the śrāvaka is empty of the vehicle of the śrāvaka. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the vehicle of the śrāvaka does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The vehicle of the pratyekabuddha is empty of the vehicle of the pratyekabuddha. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The Buddha-vehicle is empty of the Buddha-vehicle. Why is that?
For in emptiness, the Buddha-vehicle does not exist, nor does the bodhisattva. The śrāvaka is empty of the śrāvaka. Why is that?
For in emptiness, a śrāvaka is not found, nor is a bodhisattva. A pratyekabuddha is empty of a pratyekabuddha. Why is that?
For in emptiness, a pratyekabuddha is not found, nor is a bodhisattva. A Tathāgata is empty of a Tathāgata. Why is that?
For in emptiness, a Tathāgata is not found, nor is a bodhisattva.
In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, even as "form is a bodhisattva," it does not exist and is not apprehended;
even as "feeling is a bodhisattva," it does not exist and is not apprehended; even as "perception is a bodhisattva," it does not exist and is not apprehended.

The formative factors (*saṃskāra*) as a "bodhisattva"—even thus they do not exist and are not apprehended; consciousness (*vijñāna*) as a "bodhisattva"—even thus it does not exist and is not apprehended.
Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, as for what you have asked: "For what reason do you say this?"
Thus he spoke: "Since I do not perceive any bodhisattva at all—what bodhisattva shall I address and instruct in what perfection of wisdom?
O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form does not exist and is not perceived in form;
form does not exist and is not perceived in feeling."
Feeling does not exist and is not apprehended within feeling;
feeling does not exist and is not apprehended within form;
both form and feeling do not exist and are not apprehended within perception.
Perception does not exist and is not apprehended within perception; perception does not exist and is not apprehended within form and feeling;
form, feeling, and perception do not exist and are not apprehended within mental formations.
Formations do not exist and are not perceived within formations;
formations do not exist and are not perceived within form, feeling, and perception;
form, feeling, perception, and formations do not exist and are not perceived within consciousness.
Consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended in consciousness;
consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended in form, feeling, perception, or mental formations.
Furthermore, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the eye does not exist and is not apprehended in the eye.
The eye does not exist and is not apprehended in the ear; the ear does not exist and is not apprehended in the ear;
the ear does not exist and is not apprehended in the eye.
The eye and the ear do not exist and are not perceived in the nose;
the nose does not exist and is not perceived in the nose;
the nose does not exist and is not perceived in the eye and the ear.
The eye, ear, and nose do not exist and are not perceived in the tongue;
the tongue does not exist and is not perceived in the tongue;
the tongue does not exist and is not perceived in the eye, ear, and nose.
The eye, ear, nose, and tongue do not exist and are not perceived in the body;
the body does not exist and is not perceived in the body;
and the body does not exist and is not perceived in the eye, ear, nose, and tongue.
The eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body do not exist and are not apprehended in the mind; the mind does not exist and is not apprehended in the mind;
and the mind does not exist and is not apprehended in the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.
Form does not exist and is not perceived in form;
form does not exist and is not perceived in sound;
sound does not exist and is not perceived in sound.
Sound does not exist and is not perceived in form;
the word "form" does not exist and is not perceived in odor;
odor does not exist and is not perceived in odor.
Odor does not exist and is not perceived in form or sound;
form, sound, and odor do not exist and are not perceived in taste;
taste does not exist and is not perceived in taste.
Taste is neither found nor perceived among form, sound, and odor;
form, sound, odor, and taste are neither found nor perceived in touch;
and touch is neither found nor perceived in touch.

Tangibility is not found and is not perceived within form, sound, odor, and taste; form, sound, odor, taste, and tangibility are not found and are not perceived within mental phenomena (*dharmas*); and mental phenomena are not found and are not perceived within mental phenomena.
Phenomena do not exist and are not perceived within forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles.
Eye-consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within eye-consciousness;
eye-consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within ear-consciousness.
Auditory consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within auditory consciousness;
auditory consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within visual consciousness;
and both visual consciousness and auditory consciousness do not exist and are not perceived within olfactory consciousness.
Olfactory consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within olfactory consciousness;
olfactory consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within visual or auditory consciousness;
and visual, auditory, and olfactory consciousnesses do not exist and are not perceived within gustatory consciousness.
Tongue-consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within tongue-consciousness;
tongue-consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, or nose-consciousness;
and eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, and tongue-consciousness do not exist and are not perceived within body-consciousness.
Body-consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within body-consciousness;
body-consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, or mind-consciousness;
and eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness do not exist and are not perceived within mental-consciousness.
Mental consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended within mental consciousness;
mental consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended within visual, auditory, olfactory, gustatory, or tactile consciousnesses.
Visual contact does not exist and is not apprehended within visual contact.
Eye-contact does not exist and is not perceived in ear-contact;
ear-contact does not exist and is not perceived in ear-contact;
and ear-contact does not exist and is not perceived in eye-contact.
Eye-contact does not exist and is not perceived in ear-contact;
nose-contact does not exist and is not perceived in nose-contact;
and nose-contact does not exist and is not perceived in eye-contact or ear-contact.
Eye-contact does not exist and is not perceived in ear-contact; nose-contact does not exist and is not perceived in tongue-contact;
tongue-contact does not exist and is not perceived in tongue-contact;
and tongue-contact does not exist and is not perceived in eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, or tongue-contact.
Eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, and body-contact do not exist and are not apprehended in body-contact;
body-contact does not exist and is not apprehended in body-contact;
and body-contact does not exist and is not apprehended in eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, and tongue-contact.
Eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, and body-contact do not exist and are not apprehended in mind-contact;
mind-contact does not exist and is not apprehended in mind-contact;
and mind-contact does not exist and is not apprehended in eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, and body-contact.
Feeling born of eye-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within feeling born of eye-contact;
feeling born of eye-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within feeling born of ear-contact;
feeling born of ear-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within feeling born of ear-contact.
Feeling born of ear-contact does not exist and is not perceived in feeling born of eye-contact;
feeling born of eye-contact and feeling born of ear-contact do not exist and are not perceived in feeling born of nose-contact;
feeling born of nose-contact does not exist and is not perceived in feeling born of nose-contact.
Feeling born of olfactory contact does not exist and is not apprehended in feeling born of visual contact or feeling born of auditory contact;
feeling born of visual contact, feeling born of auditory contact, and feeling born of olfactory contact do not exist and are not apprehended in feeling born of gustatory contact;
feeling born of gustatory contact does not exist and is not apprehended in feeling born of gustatory contact.
Feeling born of tongue-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, or feeling born of nose-contact;
feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, and feeling born of tongue-contact do not exist and are not apprehended within feeling born of body-contact;
and feeling born of body-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within feeling born of body-contact.

The feeling born of body-contact does not exist and is not apprehended in the feeling born of eye-contact, the feeling born of ear-contact, the feeling born of nose-contact, or the feeling born of tongue-contact;

nor does the feeling born of body-contact exist in the feeling born of eye-contact, the feeling born of ear-contact, the feeling born of nose-contact, the feeling born of tongue-contact, the feeling born of body-contact, or the feeling born of mind-contact.
They do not exist and are not apprehended;
feeling born of mind-contact does not exist and is not apprehended in feeling born of mind-contact;
feeling born of mind-contact does not exist in feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, or feeling born of body-contact.
It exists, yet it is not apprehended.
The earth element does not exist and is not apprehended within the earth element;
the earth element does not exist and is not apprehended within the water element.
The water element does not exist and is not apprehended within the water element; the water element does not exist and is not apprehended within the earth element;
and both the earth element and the water element do not exist and are not apprehended within the fire element.
The fire element does not exist and is not perceived within the fire element;
the fire element does not exist and is not perceived within the earth element or the water element;
and the earth element, the water element, or the fire element does not exist and is not perceived within the wind element.
The wind element does not exist and is not apprehended within the wind element;
the wind element does not exist and is not apprehended within the earth element, the water element, or the fire element;
the earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the wind element do not exist and are not apprehended within the space element.
The space element does not exist and is not apprehended within the space element;
the space element does not exist and is not apprehended within the earth element, the water element, the fire element, or the wind element;
nor do the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the wind element, or the space element exist and are not apprehended within the consciousness element.
The consciousness element does not exist and is not perceived within the consciousness element;
the consciousness element does not exist and is not perceived within the earth element, water element, fire element, wind element, or space element.
Ignorance does not exist and is not perceived within ignorance.
Ignorance is not found and is not perceived within the formative forces; the formative forces are not found and are not perceived within the formative forces;
the formative forces are not found and are not perceived within ignorance.
Ignorance and formative predispositions do not exist and are not perceived within consciousness;
consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within consciousness;
and consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within ignorance or the formative predispositions.
Ignorance, volitional formations, and consciousness do not exist and are not apprehended within name-and-form;
name-and-form does not exist and is not apprehended within name-and-form;
and name-and-form does not exist and is not apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, and consciousness.
Ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, and name-and-form do not exist and are not apprehended in the six sense bases;
the six sense bases do not exist and are not apprehended in the six sense bases;
and the six sense bases do not exist and are not apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, and name-and-form.
Ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, and the six sense bases do not exist and are not apprehended in contact; contact does not exist and is not apprehended in contact;
and contact does not exist and is not apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, and the six sense bases.
Ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, and feeling do not exist and are not apprehended within feeling;
feeling does not exist and is not apprehended within feeling;
and feeling, ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, and contact do not exist and are not apprehended within [feeling].
Ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, and feeling do not exist and are not apprehended in craving;
craving does not exist and is not apprehended in craving;
and craving, ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, and feeling do not exist and are not apprehended [in one another].
Ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, and craving do not exist and are not perceived within grasping;
grasping does not exist and is not perceived within grasping;
and grasping does not exist and is not perceived within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, and craving.
Ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, and grasping do not exist and are not apprehended in becoming;
becoming does not exist and is not apprehended in becoming;
and becoming does not exist and is not apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, and grasping.

Ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, and becoming do not exist and are not apprehended in birth; birth does not exist and is not apprehended in birth;
and birth does not exist and is not apprehended within ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, and becoming.

Ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and aging-and-death do not exist and are not perceived in aging-and-death;
aging-and-death does not exist and is not perceived in aging-and-death;

and aging-and-death does not exist and is not perceived in ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, and birth.
The perfection of generosity does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfection of generosity;
