the perfection of generosity does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfection of ethical discipline; the perfection of ethical discipline does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfection of ethical discipline.

The perfection of ethical discipline does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfection of generosity; the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline do not exist and are not apprehended within the perfection of patience;
the perfection of patience does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfection of patience.

The perfection of patience does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfections of generosity and ethical discipline; the perfections of generosity and ethical discipline do not exist and are not apprehended within the perfection of vigor;
the perfection of vigor does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfection of vigor itself.

The perfection of vigor is not found and is not apprehended within the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, and patience; the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, and patience are not found and are not apprehended within the perfection of vigor;
and the perfection of meditation is not found and is not apprehended within the perfection of meditation.

The perfection of meditation is not found and is not apprehended within the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and vigor; the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and vigor are not found and are not apprehended within the perfection of meditation;
the perfection of wisdom is not found and is not apprehended within the perfection of wisdom.

The perfection of wisdom does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, or the perfection of meditative concentration.
Internal emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness; internal emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within external emptiness.
External emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within external emptiness;
external emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness;
internal emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within both external and internal emptiness.
Internal-external emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within internal-external emptiness;
internal-external emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness or external emptiness;
internal emptiness, external emptiness, and emptiness of emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended within the emptiness of emptiness.
The emptiness of emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within the emptiness of emptiness;

the emptiness of emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness and external emptiness; internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, and great emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended within the emptiness of emptiness.
Great emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within great emptiness;
great emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, or the emptiness of the great.

Internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, and ultimate emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended within ultimate emptiness.
Ultimate emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within ultimate emptiness;

ultimate emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, or the emptiness of the conditioned.

Internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, and the emptiness of the conditioned do not [exist] within the emptiness of the unconditioned.
They exist but are not apprehended;
conditioned emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within conditioned emptiness;

conditioned emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, or ultimate emptiness.

Internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, and unconditioned emptiness do not exist within unconditioned emptiness;
unconditioned emptiness does not exist within, nor is it apprehended within, unconditioned emptiness;

and unconditioned emptiness does not exist within internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, or unconditioned emptiness.

Internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned,
and absolute emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended; absolute emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within absolute emptiness.

In ultimate emptiness, internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate, emptiness of the conditioned, and emptiness of the unconditioned, [the self] does not exist and is not apprehended; likewise, internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, and ultimate emptiness [do not exist and are not apprehended].
They do not exist and are not apprehended in the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end;

the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end does not exist and is not apprehended in the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end; nor do they exist and are not apprehended in the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, and the absolute emptiness.

They do not exist and are not apprehended; internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of that which has no beginning or end,
and emptiness of non-dispersal do not exist and are not apprehended.
Non-dispersal emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within non-dispersal emptiness;

it does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, and the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end.

Internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, and the emptiness of non-dispersal do not exist and are not apprehended within the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature does not exist and is not apprehended within the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

In the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal and external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhā-śūnyatā*), emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the ultimate (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the beginningless and endless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), these do not exist and are not apprehended; [namely] internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal and external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the beginningless and endless, emptiness of non-dispersal, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

In the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), they do not exist and are not apprehended; the emptiness of all phenomena does not exist and is not apprehended within the emptiness of all phenomena— nor in the emptiness of internal phenomena (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of external phenomena (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of both internal and external phenomena (*adhyātmabahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), the great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the ultimate (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), or the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*).

They do not exist and are not apprehended; internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, the emptiness of non-dispersal, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of all phenomena do not exist and are not apprehended within the emptiness of specific characteristics.
The emptiness of specific characteristics does not exist and is not apprehended within the emptiness of specific characteristics;

it does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, the emptiness of non-dispersal, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of all phenomena.

In the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, the emptiness of non-dispersal, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
the emptiness of all phenomena, and the emptiness of specific characteristics, these do not exist and are not perceived.
Non-apprehension-emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within non-apprehension-emptiness;

it does not exist and is not apprehended within internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the beginningless and endless, emptiness of non-dispersal, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of all phenomena, and emptiness of specific characteristics.

Internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, the emptiness of non-dispersal, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of non-apprehension, and the emptiness of non-existence do not exist and are not apprehended;
the emptiness of non-existence does not exist and is not apprehended within the emptiness of non-existence.

In non-existence emptiness, internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the beginningless and endless, emptiness of non-dispersal, emptiness of nature, emptiness of all dharmas, emptiness of specific characteristics, and emptiness of non-apprehension, nothing exists and nothing is apprehended.

Internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the beginningless and endless, emptiness of non-dispersal, emptiness of nature, emptiness of all dharmas, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of the non-apprehendable, and the emptiness of non-existence do not exist and are not apprehended within the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature does not exist and is not apprehended within the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

In intrinsic nature emptiness, internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the beginningless and endless, emptiness of non-dispersal, emptiness of nature, emptiness of all dharmas, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of the non-apprehendable, and emptiness of non-existence, nothing exists and nothing is apprehended.

In internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the beginningless and endless, emptiness of non-dispersal, emptiness of nature, emptiness of all dharmas, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of non-apprehension, emptiness of self-nature,

and emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence, they do not exist and are not apprehended; in the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence, the emptiness of the self-nature of existence does not exist and is not apprehended.

In the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the beginningless and endless, emptiness of non-dispersal, emptiness of nature, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of non-apprehension, emptiness of existence, and emptiness of self-nature, nothing exists and nothing is apprehended.
The applications of mindfulness do not exist and are not apprehended within the applications of mindfulness.
The foundations of mindfulness do not exist and are not perceived within the right efforts;
the right efforts do not exist and are not perceived within the right efforts; the right efforts do not exist and are not perceived within the foundations of mindfulness.

The foundations of mindfulness and the right efforts do not exist and are not apprehended within the bases of psychic power; the bases of psychic power do not exist and are not apprehended within the bases of psychic power;
and the bases of psychic power do not exist and are not apprehended within the foundations of mindfulness and the right efforts.
The foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, and the bases of psychic power do not exist and are not apprehended within the faculties;
the faculties do not exist and are not apprehended within the faculties;
and the faculties do not exist and are not apprehended within the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, and the bases of psychic power.
The foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, and the faculties do not exist and are not apprehended within the powers;

the powers do not exist and are not apprehended within the powers; and the powers do not exist and are not apprehended within the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, and the faculties.
The foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, and the powers do not exist and are not apprehended within the factors of enlightenment;

the factors of enlightenment do not exist and are not apprehended within the factors of enlightenment; and the factors of enlightenment do not exist and are not apprehended within the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, and the powers.
The foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment do not exist and are not apprehended in the path;
the path does not exist and is not apprehended in the path;
and the path does not exist and is not apprehended within the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment.
The noble truths do not exist and are not apprehended within the noble truths;
the noble truths do not exist and are not apprehended within the meditative absorptions;
the meditative absorptions do not exist and are not apprehended within the meditative absorptions.
The meditative absorptions do not exist and are not perceived within the noble truths;
the noble truths and the meditative absorptions do not exist and are not perceived within the immeasurables;
the immeasurables do not exist and are not perceived within the immeasurables.
The immeasurables do not exist and are not apprehended within the noble truths and the meditative absorptions;
the noble truths, the meditative absorptions, and the immeasurables do not exist and are not apprehended within the formless attainments;
the formless attainments do not exist and are not apprehended within the formless attainments.
The formless attainments do not exist and are not apprehended within the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, and the immeasurables;
the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments do not exist and are not apprehended within the liberations;
and the liberations do not exist and are not apprehended within the liberations.
The liberations do not exist and are not apprehended within the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments;
the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, and the liberations do not exist and are not apprehended within the serial attainments.
The serial attainments do not exist and are not apprehended within the serial attainments.
The successive attainments of meditative dwelling are not found and are not apprehended within the noble truths, the dhyānas, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, and the liberations.

The noble truths, the dhyānas, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the liberations, and the successive attainments of meditative dwelling are not found and are not apprehended within the gates of liberation.
The gates of liberation are not found and are not apprehended within the gates of liberation.

The doors of liberation do not exist and are not apprehended within the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the liberations, and the serial attainments of meditative dwelling;

the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the liberations, and the serial attainments of meditative dwelling do not exist and are not apprehended within the superknowledges;
and the superknowledges do not exist and are not apprehended within the superknowledges.

The superknowledges do not exist and are not apprehended within the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the liberations, and the successive attainments of the stages of liberation;

the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the liberations, the successive attainments of the stages of liberation, and the superknowledges do not exist and are not apprehended within the meditative absorptions;
and the meditative absorptions do not exist and are not apprehended within the meditative absorptions.

The concentrations do not exist and are not apprehended within the noble truths, the meditative absorptions, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the liberations, the serial attainments, the doors of liberation, the superknowledges, and the concentrations;

the noble truths, the meditative absorptions, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the liberations, the serial attainments, the doors of liberation, the superknowledges, and the concentrations do not exist and are not apprehended within the doors of dhāraṇī; and the doors of dhāraṇī do not exist and are not apprehended within the doors of dhāraṇī.

The gateways of dhāraṇī do not exist and are not apprehended within the noble truths, the meditations, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the liberations, the serial attainments, the gateways of liberation, the superknowledges, and the concentrations.
The powers of a Tathāgata do not exist and are not apprehended within the powers of a Tathāgata;
the powers of a Tathāgata do not exist and are not apprehended within the grounds of self-confidence.

The grounds of self-confidence do not exist and are not apprehended within the grounds of self-confidence; the grounds of self-confidence do not exist and are not apprehended within the powers of a Tathāgata;
and the powers of a Tathāgata and the grounds of self-confidence do not exist and are not apprehended within the analytical knowledges.

The analytical knowledges do not exist and are not apprehended within the analytical knowledges; the analytical knowledges do not exist and are not apprehended within the powers and fearlessnesses of a Tathāgata;
and the powers, fearlessnesses, and analytical knowledges of a Tathāgata do not exist and are not apprehended within the unique qualities of a Buddha.
The unique qualities of a Buddha do not exist and are not apprehended within the unique qualities of a Buddha;

the unique qualities of a Buddha do not exist and are not apprehended within the powers, intrepidities, and analytical knowledges of a Tathāgata. The factors of the lineage do not exist and are not apprehended within the factors of the lineage.

The dharmas of the lineage (gotrabhū) do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of the eighth person; the dharmas of the eighth person do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of the eighth person;
the dharmas of the eighth person do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of the lineage.
The dharmas of the lineage-holder and the dharmas of the eighth person do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of stream-entry;
the dharmas of stream-entry do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of stream-entry;
and the dharmas of stream-entry do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of the lineage-holder and the eighth person.

The dharmas of the lineage (gotrabhū), the dharmas of the eightfold [path], and the dharmas of stream-entry (srotāpatti) do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmin); the dharmas of once-returning do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of once-returning;
and the dharmas of once-returning do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of the lineage, the eightfold path, or stream-entry.

The dharmas of the lineage (gotrabhū), the dharmas of the eighth person, the dharmas of the stream-enterer, the dharmas of the once-returner, and the dharmas of the non-returner do not exist and are not perceived within the dharmas of arhatship;
the dharmas of the non-returner do not exist and are not perceived within the dharmas of the non-returner;
and the dharmas of the non-returner do not exist and are not perceived within the dharmas of the lineage, the eighth person, the stream-enterer, or the once-returner.

The dharmas of the lineage, the dharmas of the eighth person, the dharmas of the stream-enterer, the dharmas of the once-returner, and the dharmas of the non-returner do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of the arhat;
the dharmas of the arhat do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of the arhat;

and the dharmas of the arhat do not exist and are not apprehended within the dharmas of the lineage, the dharmas of the eighth person, the dharmas of the stream-enterer, or the dharmas of the once-returner.

The dharmas of the lineage-holder (*gotrabhū*), the dharmas of the eighth-rank practitioner (*aṣṭamaka*), the dharmas of the stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*), the dharmas of the once-returner (*sakṛdāgāmin*), and the dharmas of the arhat do not exist and are not perceived within the dharmas of the pratyekabuddha;
the dharmas of the pratyekabuddha do not exist and are not perceived within the dharmas of the pratyekabuddha;

and the dharmas of the pratyekabuddha do not exist and are not perceived within the dharmas of the lineage-holder, the eighth-rank practitioner, the stream-enterer, the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat.
The stage of an ordinary person does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of an ordinary person;

the stage of an ordinary person does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of the spiritual lineage; the stage of the spiritual lineage does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of the spiritual lineage.
The stage of the lineage does not exist and is not perceived within the stage of ordinary beings;
the stage of ordinary beings and the stage of the lineage do not exist and are not perceived within the stage of the eighth person;
the stage of the eighth person does not exist and is not perceived within the stage of the eighth person.
The eighth stage does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of ordinary beings or the stage of the lineage;
the stages of ordinary beings, the stage of the lineage, and the eighth stage do not exist and are not apprehended within the stage of vision;
the stage of vision does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of vision.

The stage of vision does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of ordinary beings, the stage of the spiritual lineage, or the stage of the eighth person; the stages of ordinary beings, the stage of the spiritual lineage, and the stage of the eighth person do not exist and are not apprehended within the stage of refinement; and the stage of refinement does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of refinement itself.

The stage of the subtle (tanubhūmi) does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of ordinary beings (pṛthagjanabhūmi), the stage of the lineage (gotrabhūmi), the stage of the eighth person (aṣṭamakabhūmi), or the stage of vision (darśanabhūmi).
The stages of ordinary beings, the lineage, the eighth person, vision, and the subtle do not exist and are not apprehended within the stage of one free from passion (vītarāgabhūmi).
The stage of one free from passion does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of one free from passion.
The stage of one free from passion does not exist and is not perceived within the stages of ordinary beings, the lineage stage, the eighth stage, the stage of vision, or the stage of refinement;

likewise, the stages of ordinary beings, the lineage stage, the eighth stage, the stage of vision, the stage of refinement, and the stage of being free from passion do not exist and are not perceived within the stage of one who has completed what was to be done.
Furthermore, the stage of one who has completed what was to be done does not exist and is not perceived within the stage of one who has completed what was to be done.

The stage of one who has completed the task (*kṛtāvibhūmi*) does not exist and is not apprehended within the stages of the ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*), the lineage (*gotra*), the eighth [stage] (*aṣṭamaka*), the stage of vision (*darśana*), the stage of refinement (*tanu*), or the stage of freedom from passion (*vītarāga*);

the stages of the ordinary person, the lineage, the eighth, the stage of vision, the stage of refinement, and the stage of freedom from passion do not exist and are not apprehended within the stage of the solitary buddha (*pratyekabuddha*); and the stage of the solitary buddha does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of the solitary buddha itself.

The stage of a pratyekabuddha does not exist and is not apprehended within the stages of an ordinary person, the stage of the lineage, the stage of the eighth, the stage of seeing, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from passion, or the stage of one who has completed the task.

Likewise, the stages of an ordinary person, the stage of the lineage, the stage of the eighth, the stage of seeing, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from passion, the stage of one who has completed the task, and the stage of a pratyekabuddha do not exist and are not apprehended within the stage of a bodhisattva.
The bodhisattva stage does not exist and is not apprehended within the bodhisattva stage.

The bodhisattva stage does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of ordinary beings, the stage of the lineage, the stage of the eighth person, the stage of vision, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from passion, the stage of one who has completed the task, the stage of the pratyekabuddha, or the stage of the perfectly awakened buddha.

The stages of ordinary beings, the stage of the lineage, the stage of the eighth person, the stage of vision, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from passion, the stage of one who has completed the task, the stage of the pratyekabuddha, and the bodhisattva stage [do not exist] within the stage of the perfectly awakened buddha.
They do not exist and are not apprehended;
the stage of a perfectly awakened Buddha does not exist and is not apprehended within the stage of a perfectly awakened Buddha.

The stage of a perfectly awakened Buddha [does not exist and is not apprehended] within the stage of ordinary persons, the stage of the spiritual lineage, the stage of the eighth person, the stage of seeing, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from passion, the stage of one who has completed what was to be done, the stage of a pratyekabuddha, or the stage of a bodhisattva.
It does not exist and is not apprehended.
Omniscience does not exist and is not apprehended in omniscience; omniscience does not exist and is not apprehended in the knowledge of the aspects of the path.

The knowledge of the aspects of the path does not exist and is not apprehended within the knowledge of the aspects of the path; the knowledge of the aspects of the path does not exist and is not apprehended within the knowledge of all aspects;
and both the knowledge of all things and the knowledge of the aspects of the path do not exist and are not apprehended within the knowledge of all aspects.
The knowledge of all aspects does not exist and is not apprehended within the knowledge of all aspects;
the knowledge of all aspects does not exist and is not apprehended within the knowledge of the aspects of the path of omniscience.
The stream-enterer does not exist and is not apprehended within the state of a stream-enterer.
The stream-enterer does not exist and is not apprehended in the once-returner;
the once-returner does not exist and is not apprehended in the once-returner;
the once-returner does not exist and is not apprehended in the stream-enterer.
The stream-enterer and the once-returner do not exist and are not apprehended in the non-returner;
the non-returner does not exist and is not apprehended in the non-returner;
and the non-returner does not exist and is not apprehended in the stream-enterer and the once-returner.
The stream-enterer, the once-returner, and the non-returner do not exist and are not apprehended in the arhat;
the arhat does not exist and is not apprehended in the arhat;
and the arhat does not exist and is not apprehended among the stream-enterers, once-returners, and non-returners.
The stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, and arhat do not exist and are not apprehended in a pratyekabuddha;
a pratyekabuddha does not exist and is not apprehended in a pratyekabuddha;
and a pratyekabuddha does not exist and is not apprehended in stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, and arhats.
The stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, and pratyekabuddha do not exist and are not apprehended in the bodhisattva;
the bodhisattva does not exist and is not apprehended in the bodhisattva;
and the bodhisattva does not exist and is not apprehended in the stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, and pratyekabuddha.
The stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, pratyekabuddha, and bodhisattva do not exist and are not apprehended in the Tathāgata;
the Tathāgata does not exist and is not apprehended in the Tathāgata;
and the Tathāgata does not exist and is not apprehended in the stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, pratyekabuddha, and bodhisattvas.
A bodhisattva does not exist and is not apprehended within a bodhisattva;
a bodhisattva does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfection of wisdom;
the perfection of wisdom does not exist and is not apprehended within the perfection of wisdom.
The perfection of wisdom does not exist and is not apprehended in the bodhisattva; the bodhisattva and the perfection of wisdom do not exist and are not apprehended in the instruction and admonition;
and the instruction and admonition does not exist and is not apprehended in the instruction and admonition.
Instruction and admonition do not exist and are not apprehended in the perfection of wisdom of a bodhisattva.
Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, since all dharmas do not exist and are not apprehended, a bodhisattva does not exist and is not apprehended.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, as to what you ask: "For what reason is this merely a name, namely 'bodhisattva'? [it is because it is so].
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "bodhisattva" is adventitious and superimposed;
for that reason it is said that "bodhisattva" is merely a name.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, these designations "form," "feeling," "perception," "formative factors," and "consciousness" are adventitious and superimposed.
For indeed, that which is called a "name" comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and stays nowhere;
and that which is a mere name is not form, nor is it feeling, nor is it perception, nor are they formations, nor is it consciousness. Why is that?
Because a name is empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*); and that which is empty is not a name. For that reason, it is said that this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere name.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation is adventitious and superimposed—namely, "eye," "ear," "nose," "tongue," "body," and "mind. For a name comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and stays nowhere;
and that which is a mere name is not the eye, not the ear, not the nose, not the tongue, not the body, and not the mind. Why is that?

For indeed, that which is called "name" is empty of intrinsic nature; and that which is empty is not a name. For that reason it is said: "This so-called 'bodhisattva' is merely a designation. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation is adventitious and superimposed—namely, "form," "sound," "odor," "taste," "tangible object," and "phenomena.
For indeed, a name comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and abides nowhere.

And that which is a mere name is not form, nor is it sound, nor smell, nor taste, nor touch, nor are they mental phenomena (*dharma*). Why is that? Because a name is empty of intrinsic nature; and that which is empty is not a name. For that reason, it is said that "Bodhisattva" is merely a designation. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation is adventitious and superimposed, namely: "eye-consciousness," "ear-consciousness," "nose-consciousness," and "tongue-consciousness."
"Body-consciousness," "mind-consciousness"—
in this way, indeed, a name comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and stays nowhere;
and that which is a mere name is not eye-consciousness, not ear-consciousness, not nose-consciousness, not tongue-consciousness, not body-consciousness, and not mind-consciousness.

For what reason? Because that which is called "name" is empty of intrinsic nature, and that which is empty is not a name; for that reason it is said that this so-called "bodhisattva" is merely a designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation—namely, "eye-contact," "ear-contact," "nose-contact," or "tongue-contact"—is adventitious and has been superimposed.
Thus, "body-contact" and "mind-contact"— for indeed, that which is a mere name comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and stays nowhere;
and that which is a mere name is not eye-contact, not ear-contact, not nose-contact, not tongue-contact, not body-contact, and not mind-contact.

For what reason? Because that which is called "name" is empty of intrinsic nature, and that which is empty is not a name; for that reason it is said that this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "feeling conditioned by visual contact" is an adventitious appellation that has been superimposed.
Feeling conditioned by ear-contact, feeling conditioned by nose-contact, feeling conditioned by tongue-contact, feeling conditioned by body-contact, and feeling conditioned by mind-contact—
indeed, they do not come from anywhere, they do not go anywhere, and they do not abide anywhere.

And that which is a mere name is not the feeling conditioned by eye-contact, nor is it the feeling conditioned by ear-contact, nor is it the feeling conditioned by nose-contact, nor is it the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact, nor is it the feeling conditioned by body-contact, nor is it the feeling conditioned by mind-contact. For what reason?

For indeed, that which is called "name" is empty of intrinsic nature; and that which is empty is not a name. For that reason it is said: "This so-called 'bodhisattva' is a mere designation. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation is adventitious and superimposed—namely, "the earth element," "the water element," "the fire element," "the wind element," "the space element," and "the consciousness element."
For indeed, that which is called a "name" comes from nowhere, goes nowhere, and stays nowhere;

and that which is a mere name is not the earth element, nor the water element, nor the fire element, nor the air element, nor the space element, nor the consciousness element. Why is that? Because a name is empty by its own nature (*svabhāva*); and that which is empty is not a name. For that reason it is said: "That which is called a 'bodhisattva' is a mere name."

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation is adventitious and superimposed, namely: "ignorance," "formative forces," "consciousness," "name-and-form," "the six sense bases," "contact," "feeling," "craving," "clinging," "existence," "birth," and "old age and death."
For indeed, that which is merely a name does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere;
and that which is a mere name is not ignorance, nor those formative forces, nor that consciousness, nor that name-and-form,
nor those six sense bases, nor that contact, nor that feeling, nor that craving, nor that grasping, nor that becoming.

That is not birth, nor is that old age and death. For what reason? Because a name is empty; a name does not exist by way of its own-being (*svabhāva*). That which is empty is not a name; therefore it is called "mere designation. That is to say, "Bodhisattva" is merely a designation.

Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, this so-called "perfection of generosity" is a mere name; the perfection of generosity does not exist in the name, nor does the name exist in the perfection of generosity. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is the perfection of generosity—neither of these exists and neither is apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere name.
This so-called "perfection of ethical discipline" is a mere name; the perfection of ethical discipline is not in the name, nor is the name in the perfection of ethical discipline. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is the perfection of ethical discipline do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere name.
This so-called "perfection of patience" is a mere name; the perfection of patience does not exist in the name, nor does the name exist in the perfection of patience. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is the perfection of patience do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere name.
This so-called "perfection of vigor" is a mere designation; the perfection of vigor is not in the name, nor is the name in the perfection of vigor. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is the perfection of vigor—neither of these exists nor is it apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
This is a mere designation, namely, the perfection of meditation; yet the perfection of meditation is not in the name, nor is the name in the perfection of meditation. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is the perfection of meditation—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this is a mere designation, namely, "bodhisattva."
This so-called "perfection of wisdom" is a mere name; the perfection of wisdom is not in the name, nor is the name in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is the perfection of wisdom—neither exists nor is apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere name.

This is a mere designation, namely "internal emptiness" (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*); yet within internal emptiness there is no name, nor is there internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) in the name. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is internal emptiness—neither of these exists nor is it apprehended.
Therefore, this which is called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
This so-called "external emptiness" is a mere designation; yet within external emptiness there is no name, and within the name there is no external emptiness. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is external emptiness—neither of these exists nor is it apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is merely a name; "internal-and-external emptiness" is merely a name. Yet, within internal-and-external emptiness there is no name, nor does internal-and-external emptiness exist within the name. For what reason? Because both that which is the name and that which is internal-and-external emptiness—neither of these exists, nor is either apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is merely a name; "the emptiness of emptiness" is merely a name. In the emptiness of emptiness there is no name, and in the name there is no emptiness of emptiness. Why is that? Because both that which is the name and that which is the emptiness of emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, "bodhisattva" is a mere designation; "great emptiness" is a mere designation. Yet, there is no name within great emptiness, nor is there great emptiness within the name. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is great emptiness—neither of these exists, nor can either be apprehended.
Therefore, "bodhisattva" is a mere designation; "ultimate emptiness" is a mere designation. In ultimate emptiness there is no name, and in the name there is no ultimate emptiness. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is ultimate emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "Bodhisattva" is a mere name; "conditioned emptiness" is a mere name. In conditioned emptiness there is no name, and in the name there is no conditioned emptiness. Why is that? Because both that which is the name and that which is conditioned emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is a mere name; "unconditioned emptiness" is a mere name. Yet, in unconditioned emptiness there is no name, nor is unconditioned emptiness in the name. Why is that? Because both that which is the name and that which is unconditioned emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is merely a name; "extreme emptiness" is merely a name. In extreme emptiness there is no name, nor is extreme emptiness in the name. For what reason? Because both that which is the name and that which is extreme emptiness—neither of these exists nor is perceived.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is a mere name; "beginningless and endless emptiness" is a mere name. Yet, in beginningless and endless emptiness there is no name, nor is beginningless and endless emptiness in the name. For what reason? Because both that which is the name and that which is beginningless and endless emptiness—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is merely a name; "the emptiness of non-dispersal" is merely a name. Yet, within the emptiness of non-dispersal there is no name, nor is there the emptiness of non-dispersal in the name. Why is that? Because both that which is the name and that which is the emptiness of non-dispersal do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is merely a name; "intrinsic emptiness" is merely a name. In intrinsic emptiness there is no name, and in the name there is no intrinsic emptiness. Why is that? Because both that which is the name and that which is intrinsic emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is merely a name; "the emptiness of all phenomena" is merely a name. Yet, within the emptiness of all phenomena there is no name, nor is the emptiness of all phenomena within the name. Why is that? Because both that which is the name and that which is the emptiness of all phenomena do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is merely a name; "the emptiness of specific characteristics" is merely a name. In the emptiness of specific characteristics there is no name, and in the name there is no emptiness of specific characteristics. Why is that? Because both that which is the name and that which is the emptiness of specific characteristics do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is a mere name; "non-apprehension emptiness" is a mere name. Yet, in non-apprehension emptiness there is no name, nor is non-apprehension emptiness in the name. For what reason? Because both that which is the name and that which is non-apprehension emptiness—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is a mere designation; "the emptiness of non-existence" is a mere designation. Yet, within the emptiness of non-existence there is no name, nor is the emptiness of non-existence in the name. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is the emptiness of non-existence do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "bodhisattva" is merely a name; "intrinsic emptiness" is merely a name. Yet, within intrinsic emptiness there is no name, and in the name there is no intrinsic emptiness. Why is that? Because both that which is the name and that which is intrinsic emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended.

Therefore, "Bodhisattva" is a mere name; "the emptiness of the nature of non-existence" is a mere name. Yet, within the emptiness of the nature of non-existence there is no name, nor is the emptiness of the nature of non-existence in the name. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is the emptiness of the nature of non-existence—neither of these [exists].
It exists, yet it is not apprehended;
therefore, this which is called "bodhisattva" is a mere name.
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, this which is called "bodhisattva" is a mere name.
This designation "foundations of mindfulness" is adventitiously projected; yet there is no name in the foundations of mindfulness, nor are the foundations of mindfulness in the name. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and those which are the foundations of mindfulness—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this is merely a name, namely, "bodhisattva."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "right efforts" is adventitiously applied; yet in the right efforts there is no name, nor do the right efforts exist in the name.
Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and those which are the right efforts—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, "Bodhisattva" is merely a name.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this name "bases of psychic power" is an adventitious designation that has been superimposed; yet there is no name in the bases of psychic power, nor are the bases of psychic power in the name. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and those which are the bases of psychic power—neither of these two exists nor is it apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "faculties" is adventitiously applied; yet there is no name in the faculties, nor are the faculties in the name. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and those which are the faculties—neither of these exists, nor is either apprehended.
Therefore, "Bodhisattva" is merely a designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "powers" is adventitious and superimposed; yet within the powers there is no name, nor within the name are there powers. Why is that?
Because both the name and the powers—neither of these two exists nor is it apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere name.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "limbs of awakening" is adventitious and superimposed; yet, there is no name in the limbs of awakening, nor are the limbs of awakening in the name. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and those which are the limbs of awakening do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this which is called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "the noble eightfold path" is adventitiously applied; yet in the noble eightfold path there is no name, nor in the name is there the noble eightfold path. For what reason?
For indeed, that which is called "name" and that which is the noble eightfold path—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended; therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "noble truths" is adventitious and superimposed; yet in the noble truths there is no name, nor in the name are there the noble truths. Why is that?
For indeed, both that which is called "name" and those which are the noble truths—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended; therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is merely a designation.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "meditative concentrations" is adventitiously applied; yet in the meditative concentrations there is no name, and in the name there are no meditative concentrations. Why is that?
For indeed, both that which is called "name" and those which are the "meditative concentrations" (dhyāna) do not exist and are not apprehended;
therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "immeasurables" is adventitiously applied; yet in the immeasurables there is no name, nor are the immeasurables in the name. Why is that?
For indeed, that which is called "name" and those which are the "immeasurables"—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended;
therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this name "formless attainments" is an adventitious designation superimposed; yet in the formless attainments there is no name, nor in the name are there the formless attainments.
For what reason? Because both that which is called "name" and those formless attainments do not exist and are not apprehended; therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is merely a designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "liberations" is adventitious and superimposed; yet there is no name in the liberations, nor are there liberations in the name. Why is that?
Because both the name and the liberations do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling" is adventitious and superimposed;
yet there is no name within the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling, nor are the successive attainments of meditative dwelling within the name. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and those which are the successive attainments of meditative dwelling—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this which is called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation—namely, "the gateways to liberation that are emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness"—is adventitious and superimposed; yet there is no name in the gateways to liberation, nor are the gateways to liberation in the name. Why is that?
For indeed, both that which is called "name" and those which are the "gateways to liberation" do not exist and are not apprehended; therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "superknowledges" is adventitiously applied; yet, there is no name in the superknowledges, nor are the superknowledges in the name. Why is that?
For indeed, both that which is called "name" and those which are "superknowledges" do not exist and are not apprehended; therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "meditative concentrations" is adventitiously added; yet names do not exist within the meditative concentrations, nor do meditative concentrations exist within the name. Why is that?
For indeed, both that which is called "name" and those "concentrations" do not exist and are not apprehended;
therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is merely a designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "gateways of dhāraṇī" is adventitiously applied; yet in the gateways of dhāraṇī there is no name, nor in the name are there the gateways of dhāraṇī.
For what reason?
Because both that which is called "name" and those which are the "gateways of dhāraṇī" do not exist and are not apprehended;
therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "the ten powers of a Tathāgata" is adventitious and superimposed; yet within the powers of a Tathāgata there is no name, nor do the powers of a Tathāgata exist within the name.
Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and those which are the powers of a Tathāgata—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this which is called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "the four grounds of self-confidence" is adventitiously applied; yet in the grounds of self-confidence there is no name, nor in the name are there the grounds of self-confidence.
And why is that?
For indeed, that which is called "name" and those which are the "grounds of self-confidence"—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended;
therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "the four analytical knowledges" is adventitiously added; yet there is no name in the analytical knowledges, nor are the analytical knowledges in the name.
For what reason?
Because both that which is called "name" and those analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) do not exist and are not apprehended;
therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is merely a designation.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "great loving-kindness" is adventitiously applied; yet in great loving-kindness there is no name, nor in the name is there great loving-kindness. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is great loving-kindness do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is merely a designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "great compassion" is adventitious and superimposed; yet in great compassion there is no name, nor is there great compassion in the name. Why is that?
Because both the name and great compassion do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha" is adventitiously imputed; yet there is no name in the unique qualities of a Buddha, nor do the unique qualities of a Buddha exist in the name. Why is that?
Because both the name and the unique qualities of a Buddha—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this which is called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this designation "omniscience" is an adventitious addition; yet in omniscience there is no name, nor in the name is there omniscience. Why is that?
Because both that which is the name and that which is omniscience—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended.
Therefore, this which is called "bodhisattva" is a mere name.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this name "knowledge of the aspects of the path" is an adventitious designation that has been superimposed; yet there is no name in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, nor is there the knowledge of the aspects of the path in the name.
For what reason?

For indeed, both that which is called "name" and that which is "the knowledge of the aspects of the path" do not exist and are not apprehended; therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is a mere designation.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this name "omniscience" is an adventitious designation that has been superimposed; yet in omniscience there is no name, nor in the name is there omniscience.
For what reason?
Because both that which is called "name" and that which is "the knowledge of all aspects"—both of these do not exist and are not apprehended;
therefore, this so-called "bodhisattva" is merely a designation.
As the venerable Śāradvatīputra has said,
for what reason do you speak thus: that "self, self" is so called, yet the self is absolutely unproduced?
Just as a "sentient being" is called a "sentient being," yet in the ultimate sense a sentient being is not produced;
and just as a "living soul" is called a "living soul," yet in the ultimate sense a living soul is not produced.
Just as a "creature" is called a "creature," yet a creature is absolutely unproduced; just as a "nourisher" is called a "nourisher," yet a nourisher is absolutely unproduced;
just as a "person" is called a "person," yet a person is absolutely unproduced.
Just as a person is called a "person" yet is absolutely unproduced as a person;
just as a human being is called a "human being" yet is absolutely unproduced as a human being; just as a youth is called a "youth" yet is absolutely unproduced as a youth.

Just as one is called an "agent" (kāraka) while being ultimately unproduced as an agent; just as one is called an "experiencer" (vedaka) while being ultimately unproduced as an experiencer; just as one is called a "knower" (jānaka) while being ultimately unproduced as a knower.
Just as one who sees is called "a seer," yet a seer is ultimately unproduced; so too,
venerable Śāradvatīputra, the self does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense—
how then could there be its production?
Ultimately, a sentient being (sattva) does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could there be its production?
Ultimately, a living soul (jīva) does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could there be its production?
Ultimately, a creature (jantu) does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could there be its production?
Ultimately, a nourisher (poṣa) does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could its production occur?
Ultimately, a person (puruṣa) does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could its production occur?
Ultimately, a person-entity (pudgala) does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could its production occur?
In an ultimate sense, a human being does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could there be the production of such a one?
In an ultimate sense, a person does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could there be the production of such a one?
In an ultimate sense, an agent does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could there be the production of such a one?
Ultimately, an experiencer does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could there be the production of such a one?
Ultimately, a knower does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could there be the production of such a one?
Ultimately, a seer does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could there be the production of such a one?
Ultimately, form does not exist and is not perceived; how, then, could its production occur?
Ultimately, feeling does not exist and is not perceived; how, then, could its production occur?
Ultimately, perception does not exist and is not perceived; how, then, could its production occur?
Ultimately, formative forces do not exist and are not perceived; how, then, could their production occur?

Ultimately, consciousness does not exist and is not perceived; how, then, could its production occur? Ultimately, the eye does not exist and is not perceived; how, then, could its production occur? Ultimately, the ear does not exist and is not perceived; how, then, [could its production occur]? (ŚsP_II-1_101)

How could there be the manifestation of this? Since the nose absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended, how could there be its manifestation? Since the tongue absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended, how could there be its manifestation? Since the body absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended, how could there be its manifestation?
Ultimately, the mind does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur?

Ultimately, form does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur? Ultimately, sound does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur? Ultimately, odor...

It does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur? Taste absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur? Tangible objects absolutely do not exist and are not apprehended;
how, then, could their production occur? Mental phenomena absolutely do not exist and are not apprehended.
From where will its production come about?
Since eye-consciousness absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended, from where will its production come about?
Since ear-consciousness absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended, from where will its production come about?
Ultimately, olfactory consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur?
Ultimately, gustatory consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur?
Ultimately, tactile consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur?
Since mental consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could its production ever occur?
Since visual contact does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could its production ever occur?
Since auditory contact does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could its production ever occur?
In an absolute sense, olfactory contact does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur?
In an absolute sense, gustatory contact does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur?
In an absolute sense, tactile contact does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur?
Since mental contact does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could its production occur?

Since feeling born of visual contact does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could its production occur? Since feeling born of auditory contact does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could [its production occur]?

There will be no production of this. Since, in an absolute sense, feeling born of nose-contact does not exist and is not apprehended, how could there be its production? Since, in an absolute sense, feeling born of tongue-contact does not exist and is not apprehended, how could there be its production? [Since, in an absolute sense, feeling] born of body-contact...

Feeling does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, will its production come to be? Mental-feeling born of mind-contact does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense; how, then, will its production come to be?
The earth element does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense; how, then, will its production come to be?

Ultimately, the water element does not exist and is not perceived; how then could its production occur? Ultimately, the fire element does not exist and is not perceived; how then could its production occur? Ultimately, the wind element does not exist and is not perceived; how then could its production occur? Ultimately, the space element...

It does not exist and is not apprehended; how then will its production come to be? The consciousness element (*vijñānadhātu*) absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended; how then will its production come to be?
Ignorance (*avidyā*) absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended; how then will its production come to be? Absolutely...

Formations do not exist and are not perceived; how then will their production come about? Name-and-form absolutely does not exist and is not perceived; how then will its production come about? The six sense bases absolutely do not exist and are not perceived; how then will their production come about? Absolutely...

Contact does not exist and is not perceived; how then will its production come to be? Feeling absolutely does not exist and is not perceived; how then will its production come to be? Craving absolutely does not exist and is not perceived;
how then will its production come to be? Grasping absolutely does not exist...

They do not exist and are not apprehended; how then will their production occur? Existence (*bhava*) does not exist and is not apprehended in an absolute sense; how then will its production occur? Birth (*jāti*) does not exist and is not apprehended in an absolute sense; how then will its production occur? Old age and death (*jarāmaraṇa*) do not exist in an absolute sense.
Since it is not apprehended, how could its production occur?

The perfection of generosity does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense; how could its production occur? The perfection of ethical discipline does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense; how could its production occur?
Since the perfection of patience does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could its production occur?
Since the perfection of vigor does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could its production occur?
Since the perfection of meditation does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could its production occur?
Ultimately, the perfection of wisdom does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could there be its production?

Ultimately, internal emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could there be its production? Ultimately, external emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could there be its production? Ultimately, internal-and-external emptiness...

It does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could its production occur? Ultimate emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could its production occur? Great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*) does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense; how then could its production occur? Ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*) [does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense...]

It does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur? Conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*) absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur? Unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*) absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended; how, then, could its production occur? Absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) absolutely...

It does not exist and is not perceived; how then could its production occur? Absolute beginningless and endless emptiness (*atyantānavarāgra-śūnyatā*) does not exist and is not perceived; how then could its production occur? Absolute non-dispersal emptiness (*atyantānavakāra-śūnyatā*) does not exist and is not perceived; how then could its production occur? Absolute natural emptiness (*atyanta-prakṛti-śūnyatā*)...

It does not exist and is not apprehended; how then will its production come about? Absolute emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*) does not exist and is not apprehended; how then will its production come about? Absolute emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*) does not exist and is not apprehended; how then will its production come about? Absolute emptiness of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*)...

They do not exist and are not apprehended; how then could there be the production of this? Absolute non-existence emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could there be the production of this? Absolute self-nature emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended; how then could there be the production of this? Absolute non-existence-and-self-nature emptiness...
It does not exist and is not apprehended; from where, then, will its production come?
In an absolute sense, the foundations of mindfulness do not exist and are not apprehended; from where, then, will their production come?
In an absolute sense, the right efforts do not exist and are not apprehended; from where, then, will their production come?

They will exist. Since the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) do not exist and are not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could there be their production? Since the faculties (*indriya*) do not exist and are not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could there be their production? Since the powers (*bala*) do not exist and are not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could there be their production?

It will come to be. Since the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*) absolutely do not exist and are not apprehended, how could their production occur? Since the noble eightfold path absolutely does not exist and is not apprehended, how could its production occur? Since the noble truths absolutely do not exist and are not apprehended, how could their production occur?

They will come to be. Since the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*) do not exist and are not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could their production occur? Since the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) do not exist and are not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could their production occur? Since the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*) do not [exist] in an ultimate sense...

They do not exist and are not apprehended; from where, then, will their production come? The eight liberations absolutely do not exist and are not apprehended; from where, then, will their production come? The nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling absolutely do not exist and are not apprehended; from where, then, will their production come? The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—absolutely do not exist and are not apprehended.

They do not exist and are not apprehended; how then could their production occur? The supernormal knowledges (*abhijñā*) do not exist and are not apprehended in an ultimate sense; how then could their production occur? The meditative concentrations (*samādhi*) do not exist and are not apprehended in an ultimate sense; how then could their production occur? The gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*) [do not exist and are not apprehended in an ultimate sense; how then could their production occur?]

They do not exist and are not apprehended; from where, then, will their production come? The ten powers of a Tathāgata absolutely do not exist and are not apprehended; from where, then, will their production come? The four grounds of self-confidence absolutely do not exist and are not apprehended; from where, then, will their production come? Absolutely...
The four analytical knowledges do not exist and are not apprehended; how then will they come into being?
Great loving-kindness does not exist and is not apprehended in its ultimate nature; how then will it come into being?
Great compassion does not exist and is not apprehended in its ultimate nature; how then will it come into being?

Since, in an ultimate sense, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha do not exist and are not apprehended, how could their production come to be? Since, in an ultimate sense, a Śrāvaka does not exist and is not apprehended, how could his production come to be?
Since, in an ultimate sense, a Pratyekabuddha does not exist and is not apprehended, how could his production come to be?

It will come to be. Since a bodhisattva does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could there be the manifestation of one? Since a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha does not exist and is not apprehended in an ultimate sense, how could there be the manifestation of one?
By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is said that "self" exists, yet the self is also an absolute non-arising.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, as to what you have said—that all phenomena are without intrinsic nature—it is even so, venerable Śāradvatīputra. Why is that?
For it is thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra: there is no inherent nature produced by combination.
Śāradvatīputra asked:
"Of what, venerable Subhūti, is there no inherent nature produced by combination?"

He said: "Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form has no inherent nature produced by combination; feeling has no inherent nature produced by combination; perception has no inherent nature produced by combination."
Conditioned phenomena have no inherent nature produced by conjunction;
consciousness has no inherent nature produced by conjunction.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the eye has no inherent nature produced by combination; the ear has no inherent nature produced by combination;
the nose has no inherent nature produced by combination.
The tongue has no inherent nature produced by combination; the body has no inherent nature produced by combination;
the mind has no inherent nature produced by combination.
Form has no inherent nature produced by conjunction; sound has no inherent nature produced by conjunction; odor has no inherent nature produced by conjunction.
