Consciousness is purified, not through the departure of anything; name-and-form is purified, not through the departure of anything;
the six sense bases are purified, not through the departure of anything.
Contact is purified, yet not through the departure of anything; feeling is purified, yet not through the departure of anything;
craving is purified, yet not through the departure of anything.
Grasping is purified, yet not by the departure of anything; existence is purified, yet not by the departure of anything;
birth is purified, yet not by the departure of anything.

Old age and death are purified, yet not by the departure of anything whatsoever. The perfection of generosity, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is purified, yet not by the departure of anything whatsoever; the perfection of ethical discipline is purified, yet not by the departure of anything whatsoever.
The perfection of patience is purified, yet not through the departure of anything; the perfection of vigor is purified, yet not through the departure of anything;
the perfection of meditation is purified, yet not through the departure of anything.
The perfection of wisdom is purified, yet not by the departure of anything. Noble Śāradvatīputra, internal emptiness is purified, yet not by the departure of anything;
external emptiness is purified, yet not by the departure of anything.
Internal-external emptiness is purified, yet not by the departure of anything; the emptiness of emptiness is purified, yet not by the departure of anything;
great emptiness is purified, yet not by the departure of anything.
Ultimate emptiness is purified, yet not by the departure of anything; conditioned emptiness is purified, yet not by the departure of anything;
unconditioned emptiness is purified, yet not by the departure of anything.
The emptiness of the ultimate is purified, not by the departure of anything; the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is purified, not by the departure of anything;
the emptiness of non-dispersal is purified, not by the departure of anything.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, not through the departure of anything; the emptiness of all phenomena is pure, not through the departure of anything;
the emptiness of specific characteristics is pure, not through the departure of anything.
The emptiness of non-apprehension is purified, yet not by the departure of anything; the emptiness of non-existence is purified, yet not by the departure of anything;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature is purified, yet not by the departure of anything.

The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is purified, yet not by way of the departure of anything. O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the applications of mindfulness are purified, yet not by way of the departure of anything;
the right efforts are purified, yet not by way of the departure of anything.
The bases of psychic power are purified, yet not through the departure of anything; the faculties are purified, yet not through the departure of anything;
the powers are purified, yet not through the departure of anything.
The factors of enlightenment are purified, yet not through the departure of anything;
the noble eightfold path is purified, yet not through the departure of anything. The noble truths, venerable Śāradvatīputra, are purified, yet not through the departure of anything.
The meditative absorptions are purified, yet not through the departure of anything; the immeasurables are purified, yet not through the departure of anything;
the formless attainments are purified, yet not through the departure of anything.
The eight liberations are purified, yet not by the departure of anything;

the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are purified, yet not by the departure of anything; the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are purified, yet not by the departure of anything.
The superknowledges are purified, yet not through the departure of anything; the meditative concentrations are purified, yet not through the departure of anything;
the gateways of the dhāraṇīs are purified, yet not through the departure of anything.
The ten powers of a Tathāgata are purified, yet not through the departure of anything; the four grounds of self-confidence are purified, yet not through the departure of anything;
the four analytical knowledges are purified, yet not through the departure of anything.
Great loving-kindness is purified, yet not through the departure of anything; great compassion is purified, yet not through the departure of anything;
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are purified, yet not through the departure of anything. For what reason?

For it is thus, Venerable Śāradvatīputra: that which is purified is non-existence and exhaustion. By this method, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, all phenomena are purified, yet there is nothing further for anyone, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, such that all phenomena are supramundane through the departure of anything whatsoever. He asked: "Venerable Subhūti, what are those all phenomena that are supramundane and not through the departure of anything whatsoever?"

He said: "Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form is supramundane and not through the departure of anything; feeling is supramundane and not through the departure of anything; perception is supramundane and not through the departure of anything."
Formations are supramundane, yet not through the departure of anything;
consciousness is supramundane, yet not through the departure of anything. The eye, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is supramundane, yet not through the departure of anything.
The supramundane ear does not exist through the departure of anything;
the supramundane nose does not exist through the departure of anything.
The tongue is supramundane, yet not by the departure of anything;
the body is supramundane, yet not by the departure of anything; the mind is supramundane, yet not by the departure of anything.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form is supramundane and not through the departure of anything; sound is supramundane and not through the departure of anything;
odor is supramundane and not through the departure of anything.
Taste is supramundane and not through the departure of anything; touch is supramundane and not through the departure of anything; phenomena are supramundane and not through the departure of anything.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, eye-consciousness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything; ear-consciousness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything;
nose-consciousness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything.
Tongue-consciousness is supramundane, not by the departure of anything; body-consciousness is supramundane, not by the departure of anything;
mind-consciousness is supramundane, not by the departure of anything.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, eye-contact is supramundane and does not come about through the departure of anything; ear-contact is supramundane and does not come about through the departure of anything;
nose-contact is supramundane and does not come about through the departure of anything.

Tongue-contact is supramundane, yet not through the disappearance of anything; body-contact is supramundane, yet not through the disappearance of anything; mind-contact is supramundane, yet not through the disappearance of anything.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, feeling conditioned by eye-contact is supramundane and not through the departure of anything; feeling conditioned by ear-contact is supramundane and not through the departure of anything;
feeling conditioned by nose-contact is supramundane and not through the departure of anything.

Feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything; feeling conditioned by body-contact is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything;
feeling conditioned by mind-contact is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the earth element is supramundane and does not come about through the departure of anything; the water element is supramundane and does not come about through the departure of anything;
the fire element is supramundane and does not come about through the departure of anything.
The wind element is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything; the space element is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything;
the consciousness element is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything.
Ignorance, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything; the formative forces are supramundane and do not arise through the departure of anything;
consciousness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything.
Name-and-form is supramundane and not through the disappearance of anything; the six sense bases are supramundane and not through the disappearance of anything;
contact is supramundane and not through the disappearance of anything.
Feeling is supramundane and not through the disappearance of anything; craving is supramundane and not through the disappearance of anything;
grasping is supramundane and not through the disappearance of anything.
Supramundane existence does not come about through the departure of anything;
supramundane birth does not come about through the departure of anything.
Old age and death are supramundane, and not through the disappearance of anything.
The perfection of generosity, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is supramundane, and not through the disappearance of anything;
the perfection of ethical discipline is supramundane, and not through the disappearance of anything.
The perfection of patience is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything; the perfection of vigor is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything;
the perfection of meditation is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything.
The perfection of wisdom is supramundane, and not by the departure of anything whatsoever.
Noble Śāradvatīputra, internal emptiness is supramundane, and not by the departure of anything whatsoever;
external emptiness is supramundane, and not by the departure of anything whatsoever.
Internal-external emptiness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything; the emptiness of emptiness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything;
great emptiness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything.
Ultimate emptiness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything; conditioned emptiness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything;
unconditioned emptiness is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything.
The emptiness of the ultimate is supramundane and does not occur through the disappearance of anything;
the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is supramundane and does not occur through the disappearance of anything;
the emptiness of non-dispersal is supramundane and does not occur through the disappearance of anything.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything;

the emptiness of all phenomena is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything; the emptiness of specific characteristics is supramundane and does not arise through the departure of anything.
The emptiness of non-apprehension is supramundane and does not arise through the disappearance of anything;

the emptiness of non-existence is supramundane and does not arise through the disappearance of anything; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is supramundane and does not arise through the disappearance of anything.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is supramundane, and not by the departure of anything.
O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the applications of mindfulness are supramundane, and not by the departure of anything;
the right efforts are supramundane, and not by the departure of anything.
The bases of supernatural power are supramundane and not through the departure of anything; the faculties are supramundane and not through the departure of anything;
the powers are supramundane and not through the departure of anything.
The factors of enlightenment are supramundane, yet not by way of the departure of anything;
the noble eightfold path is supramundane, yet not by way of the departure of anything. The noble truths, venerable Śāradvatīputra, are supramundane, yet not by way of the departure of anything.
The supramundane meditative absorptions do not exist through the departure of anything; the supramundane immeasurables do not exist through the departure of anything;
the supramundane formless attainments do not exist through the departure of anything.
The eight liberations are supramundane and do not arise through the departure of anything;

the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are supramundane and do not arise through the departure of anything; the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are supramundane and do not arise through the departure of anything.
The supramundane superknowledges do not arise through the departure of anything; the supramundane meditative concentrations do not arise through the departure of anything;
the supramundane doors of dhāraṇī do not arise through the departure of anything.
The ten supramundane powers of a Tathāgata do not arise through the disappearance of anything; the four supramundane grounds of self-confidence do not arise through the disappearance of anything;
the four supramundane analytical knowledges do not arise through the disappearance of anything.
Supramundane great loving-kindness does not arise through the departure of anything; supramundane great compassion does not arise through the departure of anything;
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are supramundane and do not arise through the departure of anything. For what reason?

For it is thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra: that which is supramundane is non-existence and exhaustion. By this method, venerable Śāradvatīputra, all dharmas are supramundane, yet furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, all dharmas are unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) and not by the departure of anything. He asked: "Venerable Subhūti, which are all those dharmas that are unconditioned and not by the departure of anything?"

He said: "Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form is unconditioned and not through the departure of anything; feeling is unconditioned and not through the departure of anything; perception is unconditioned and not through the departure of anything."
Formations are unconditioned and not through the disappearance of anything;
consciousness is unconditioned and not through the disappearance of anything. The eye, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is supramundane and not through the disappearance of anything.
The ear is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything;
the nose is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything; the tongue is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything.
The body is unconditioned and does not exist through the departure of anything;
the mind is unconditioned and does not exist through the departure of anything. Form, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is unconditioned and does not exist through the departure of anything.

Sound is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything; odor is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything; taste is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything.
Contact is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything; phenomena are unconditioned and do not arise through the departure of anything.
Eye-consciousness, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything.
Auditory consciousness is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything;
olfactory consciousness is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything; gustatory consciousness is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything.
Body-consciousness is unconditioned and not through the departure of anything;
mind-consciousness is unconditioned and not through the departure of anything. Eye-contact, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is unconditioned and not through the departure of anything.
Auditory contact is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything; olfactory contact is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything;
gustatory contact is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything.
Body-contact is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything; mind-contact is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, feeling conditioned by eye-contact is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything.

The conditioned sensation conditioned by auditory contact is not through the departure of anything; the conditioned sensation conditioned by olfactory contact is not through the departure of anything;
the conditioned sensation conditioned by gustatory contact is not through the departure of anything.
Feeling conditioned by bodily contact is unconditioned, yet not through the departure of anything; feeling conditioned by mental contact is unconditioned, yet not through the departure of anything.
The earth element, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is unconditioned, yet not through the departure of anything.
The water element is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything; the fire element is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything;
the wind element is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything.
The space element is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything;
the consciousness element is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything.
Ignorance, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything.
Formations are unconditioned and not through the disappearance of anything; consciousness is unconditioned and not through the disappearance of anything;
name-and-form is unconditioned and not through the disappearance of anything.
The six sense bases are unconditioned and not through the disappearance of anything; contact is unconditioned and not through the disappearance of anything;
feeling is unconditioned and not through the disappearance of anything.
Craving is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything; grasping is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything;
becoming is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything.
Birth is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything;
old age and death are unconditioned and do not exist through the disappearance of anything.
The perfection of generosity, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is unconditioned and does not exist through the disappearance of anything.

The perfection of ethical discipline is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything; the perfection of patience is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything;
the perfection of vigor is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything.
The perfection of meditation is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything; the perfection of wisdom is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything.
Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, inner emptiness is unconditioned and does not arise through the departure of anything.
External emptiness is unconditioned and does not exist through the departure of anything;
internal-external emptiness is unconditioned and does not exist through the departure of anything; the emptiness of emptiness is unconditioned and does not exist through the departure of anything.
Great emptiness is unconditioned, not by way of the departure of anything; ultimate emptiness is unconditioned, not by way of the departure of anything;
conditioned emptiness is unconditioned, not by way of the departure of anything.
Unconditioned emptiness is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything; absolute emptiness is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything;
emptiness without beginning or end is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything.
The emptiness of non-dispersal is unconditioned, not by way of the departure of anything;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature is unconditioned, not by way of the departure of anything.

The emptiness of all phenomena is unconditioned, not by way of the disappearance of anything; the emptiness of specific characteristics is unconditioned, not by way of the disappearance of anything; the emptiness of non-apprehension is unconditioned, not by way of the disappearance of anything.

The emptiness of non-existence is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything;
the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the foundations of mindfulness are unconditioned and do not exist through the departure of anything;
the right efforts are unconditioned and do not exist through the departure of anything; the bases of psychic power are unconditioned and do not exist through the departure of anything.
The faculties are unconditioned and do not arise through the departure of anything; the powers are unconditioned and do not arise through the departure of anything;
the factors of enlightenment are unconditioned and do not arise through the departure of anything.
The noble eightfold path is unconditioned, and not by the disappearance of anything. The noble truths, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, are unconditioned, and not by the disappearance of anything;
the meditative absorptions are unconditioned, and not by the disappearance of anything;
the immeasurables are unconditioned, and not by the disappearance of anything.
The formless attainments are unconditioned and do not exist through the departure of anything;

the eight liberations are unconditioned and do not exist through the departure of anything; the nine successive meditative attainments are unconditioned and do not exist through the departure of anything.
The doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are unconditioned, yet they do not exist through the departure of anything;
the superknowledges are unconditioned, yet they do not exist through the departure of anything;
the meditative concentrations are unconditioned, yet they do not exist through the departure of anything.

The gateways of dhāraṇī are unconditioned and do not exist through the disappearance of anything; the ten powers of a Tathāgata are unconditioned and do not exist through the disappearance of anything;
the four grounds of self-confidence are unconditioned and do not exist through the disappearance of anything.

The four analytical knowledges are unconditioned and do not arise through the disappearance of anything; great loving-kindness is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything;
great compassion is unconditioned and does not arise through the disappearance of anything.
The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) and do not exist through the disappearance of anything. Why is that?

Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is unconditioned is non-existence and cessation. In this manner, venerable Śāradvatīputra, all phenomena (*sarvadharma*) are unconditioned; furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, all phenomena are neither immutable nor indestructible.
He asked: "Why, venerable Subhūti, are all dharmas neither fixed nor subject to destruction?
Subhūti replied:
"Form, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is neither fixed nor subject to destruction. For what reason?"
This is its very nature: feeling is stable and indestructible. For what reason?
This is its very nature.
Perception is neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that?
Because this is its very nature:
conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that?
This is their nature: consciousness is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that?
Because this is its very nature.
The eye, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? Because this is its very nature.
The ear is neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? Because this is its very nature.
This is its very nature:
the sense of smell is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that?
This is its very nature.
The tongue is neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that?
Because such is its nature; the body is neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that?
This is its very nature: the mind is not immutable, yet it is indestructible. For what reason?
This is its very nature.

Form, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because such is its nature. Sound is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because such is its nature. Odor is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because such is its nature.

This is its very nature. Taste is not immutable and is indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. Touch is not immutable and is indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. Phenomena are not immutable and are indestructible. For what reason?
This is their intrinsic nature.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, visual consciousness is immovable and indestructible. Why is that?
Because this is its intrinsic nature. Auditory consciousness is immovable and indestructible. Why is that?
This is its very nature. Nose-consciousness is neither immutable nor indestructible.

Why is that? This is its very nature. Tongue-consciousness is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? This is its very nature. Body-consciousness is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? This is its very nature.
This is its very nature. Mental consciousness is neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason?
This is its very nature. Eye-contact, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason?

This is its very nature. Auditory contact is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. Olfactory contact is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. Gustatory contact is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature.
This is its very nature: body-contact is neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. Mind-contact is neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that?
Because this is its very nature.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, feeling conditioned by eye-contact is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. Feeling conditioned by ear-contact is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. Feeling conditioned by nose-contact is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? (ŚsP_II-1_143)

This is its very nature: the sensation conditioned by tongue-contact is immovable and indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. The sensation conditioned by body-contact is immovable and indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. The sensation conditioned by mind-contact is immovable and indestructible. For what reason?
This is its very nature.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the earth element is unchanging and indestructible. For what reason? Because this is its very nature. The water element is unchanging and indestructible. For what reason? Because this is its very nature.
This is its very nature. The fire element is immutable and indestructible. For what reason?
This is its very nature. The wind element is immutable and indestructible. For what reason?
This is its very nature. The space element is immutable and indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. The consciousness element is immutable and indestructible. Why is that?
Because this is its very nature.

Ignorance, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. Formative forces (*saṃskāra*) are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their very nature. Consciousness (*vijñāna*) is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature.

This is its very nature. Name-and-form is neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. The six sense-bases are neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. Contact is neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason?

This is its very nature: feeling is neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. Craving is neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. Grasping is neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that?

This is its very nature. Existence (*bhava*) is neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. Birth (*jāti*) is neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. Old age and death (*jarāmaraṇa*) are neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature.

This is its very nature, Venerable Śāradvatīputra: the perfection of generosity is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. The perfection of ethical discipline is neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature.
This is its nature: the perfection of patience is immovable and indestructible. For what reason?
This is its nature. The perfection of vigor is immovable and indestructible. For what reason?

This is its very nature: the perfection of meditation is immovable and indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. The perfection of wisdom is immovable and indestructible. Why is that?
Because this is its very nature.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, internal emptiness is neither fixed nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because such is its very nature. External emptiness is neither fixed nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because such is its very nature. Internal-and-external emptiness is neither fixed nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because such is its very nature.

This is its very nature: it is the emptiness of emptiness, immovable and indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. It is the great emptiness, immovable and indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. It is the emptiness of the ultimate truth, immovable and indestructible. For what reason?
This is its very nature: unconditioned emptiness is immutable and indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. Unconditioned emptiness is immutable and indestructible.
For what reason? This is its very nature. Absolute emptiness is immutable and indestructible. For what reason?

This is its very nature: it is the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, immovable and indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. It is the emptiness of non-dispersal, immovable and indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. It is the emptiness of intrinsic nature, immovable and indestructible. For what reason?

This is its very nature: the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), which is immovable and indestructible. For what reason? Because this is its very nature. It is the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), which is immovable and indestructible. For what reason? Because this is its very nature. It is the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), which is immovable and indestructible. For what reason?

This is its nature: emptiness of non-existence, which is immutable and indestructible. For what reason? This is its nature. Emptiness of intrinsic nature, which is immutable and indestructible. For what reason? This is its nature. Emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, which is immutable and indestructible. For what reason?
This is its very nature.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the foundations of mindfulness are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature. The right efforts are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature.

This is their very nature: the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? This is their very nature. The faculties (*indriya*) are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? This is their very nature. The powers (*bala*) are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? This is their very nature.

This is their very nature: the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*) are neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is their very nature. The noble eightfold path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*) is neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the noble truths (*āryasatya*) are neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason?

This is their nature: the meditative absorptions (dhyāna) are not immutable and are indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature. The immeasurables (apramāṇa) are not immutable and are indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature. The formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are not immutable and are indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature.

This is their nature: the eight liberations are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature. The nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature. The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that?

This is their nature: the superknowledges are neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that? This is their nature. The meditative concentrations are neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that? This is their nature. The gateways of the dhāraṇīs are neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that?

This is their intrinsic nature: the ten powers of a Tathāgata are neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their intrinsic nature. The four grounds of self-confidence are neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their intrinsic nature. The four analytical knowledges are neither fixed nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their intrinsic nature.
This is their nature: great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), which is neither immutable nor subject to destruction. For what reason?
Because this is its very nature. Great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is neither immutable nor subject to destruction. For what reason?
This is its very nature: the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma) are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature.
Wholesome phenomena (kuśala-dharma) are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that?

This is their nature: unwholesome phenomena are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature. Conditioned phenomena are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature. Unconditioned phenomena are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their nature.

This is their nature: contaminated phenomena (*sāsrava-dharma*) are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? This is their nature. Uncontaminated phenomena (*anāsrava-dharma*) are neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? This is their nature. By this method, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, all phenomena have non-existence as their intrinsic nature (*abhāva-svabhāva*).

At that time, one does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate ear-contact as "this is ear-contact.
At that time, one does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate nose-contact as "this is nose-contact.
At that time, one does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate tongue-contact as "this is tongue-contact."
At that time, one does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, become attached to, or designate bodily contact as "this is bodily contact.
At that time, one does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, become attached to, or designate mental contact as "this is mental contact.
At that time, one does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, become attached to, or designate feeling conditioned by visual contact as "this is feeling conditioned by visual contact."

At that time, one does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate the feeling conditioned by ear-contact, thinking, "This is the feeling conditioned by ear-contact. At that time, one does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate the feeling conditioned by nose-contact, thinking, "This is the feeling conditioned by nose-contact."

At that time, one does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact as "this is the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact.

At that time, one does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate the feeling conditioned by body-contact as "this is the feeling conditioned by body-contact."

At that time, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate the feeling conditioned by mental contact as "this is the feeling conditioned by mental contact.
Blessed One, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom examines these phenomena in this way,
at that time he does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate the perfection of giving as "this is the perfection of giving."
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the perfection of ethical discipline as "this is the perfection of ethical discipline";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the perfection of patience as "this is the perfection of patience";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the perfection of vigor as "this is the perfection of vigor."
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the perfection of meditation as "this is the perfection of meditation.
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the perfection of wisdom as "this is the perfection of wisdom.
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate internal emptiness as "this is internal emptiness."
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate external emptiness as "this is external emptiness";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate internal-external emptiness as "this is internal-external emptiness";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the emptiness of emptiness as "this is the emptiness of emptiness."
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate great emptiness as "this is great emptiness";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate ultimate emptiness as "this is ultimate emptiness";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate conditioned emptiness as "this is conditioned emptiness."
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate unconditioned emptiness as "this is unconditioned emptiness";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate absolute emptiness as "this is absolute emptiness";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate emptiness without beginning or end as "this is emptiness without beginning or end."
Thus, at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, become attached to, or designate non-dispersal emptiness as "this is non-dispersal emptiness";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, become attached to, or designate natural emptiness as "this is natural emptiness";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, become attached to, or designate the emptiness of all phenomena as "this is the emptiness of all phenomena."
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, or become attached to the emptiness of specific characteristics, nor does he designate it as "this is the emptiness of specific characteristics.
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, or become attached to the emptiness of non-apprehension, nor does he designate it as "this is the emptiness of non-apprehension.
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, or become attached to the emptiness of non-existence, nor does he designate it as "this is the emptiness of non-existence."
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate "this is the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate "this is the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Furthermore, Blessed One, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the applications of mindfulness.
At that time, thinking "these are the applications of mindfulness," he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, become attached to, or designate them as "these are the right efforts.
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, become attached to, or designate the bases of psychic power, thinking "these are the bases of psychic power."
At that time, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not preside over, does not adhere to, and does not designate the sense-faculties as "these are the sense-faculties";
at that time, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not preside over, does not adhere to, and does not designate the powers as "these are the powers";
at that time, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not preside over, does not adhere to, and does not designate the factors of enlightenment as "these are the factors of enlightenment."
At that time, one does not approach, does not take up, does not dwell upon, does not adhere to, and does not designate the noble eightfold path as "the noble eightfold path.
At that time, one does not approach, does not take up, does not dwell upon, does not adhere to, and does not designate the noble truths as "these are the noble truths.
At that time, one does not approach, does not take up, does not dwell upon, does not adhere to, and does not designate the meditative absorptions as "these are the meditative absorptions."
At that time, one does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the immeasurables as "these are the immeasurables";
at that time, one does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the formless attainments as "these are the formless attainments";
at that time, one does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, adhere to, or designate the eight liberations as "the eight liberations."

"These are [the nine successive attainments]"—at that time, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate the nine successive attainments as "these are the nine successive attainments.

At that time, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as "the gateways to liberation: emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness."
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, or adhere to supernormal knowledges, nor does he designate them as "these are supernormal knowledges.
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, or adhere to meditative concentrations, nor does he designate them as "these are meditative concentrations.
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, dwell upon, or adhere to the gateways of mnemonic formulas, nor does he designate them as "these are gateways of mnemonic formulas."
At that time, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not adhere to, and does not designate the ten powers of a Tathāgata as "these are the ten powers of a Tathāgata.

At that time, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not adhere to, and does not designate the four grounds of self-confidence as "these are the four grounds of self-confidence.
At that time, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not adhere to, and does not designate the four analytical knowledges as "these are the four analytical knowledges."
At that time, he does not approach, grasp, abide in, adhere to, or designate great loving-kindness as "this is great loving-kindness";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, abide in, adhere to, or designate great compassion as "this is great compassion";
at that time, he does not approach, grasp, abide in, adhere to, or designate the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as "these are the unique qualities of a Buddha."

Furthermore, Blessed One, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not approach, does not grasp, does not dwell upon, does not become attached to, and does not designate the gateways of all samādhis and dhāraṇīs, thinking, "These are the gateways of all samādhis and dhāraṇīs. For what reason?
For in this way, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not perceive form,
he does not perceive feeling, and he does not perceive perception.
He does not perceive volitional formations;
he does not perceive consciousness.
He does not perceive the eye.
He does not perceive the ear;
he does not perceive the nose;
he does not perceive the tongue.
He does not perceive the body;
he does not perceive the mind.
He does not perceive form.
He does not perceive sound, he does not perceive odor,
he does not perceive taste.
He does not perceive contact; he does not perceive mental phenomena.
He does not perceive eye-consciousness.
He does not perceive auditory consciousness;
he does not perceive olfactory consciousness;
he does not perceive gustatory consciousness.
One does not perceive body-consciousness,
nor does one perceive mind-consciousness. One does not perceive eye-contact.
He does not perceive auditory contact; he does not perceive olfactory contact;
he does not perceive gustatory contact.
One does not perceive body-contact;
one does not perceive mind-contact.
One does not perceive feeling conditioned by eye-contact.
He does not perceive feeling conditioned by auditory contact;
he does not perceive feeling conditioned by olfactory contact;
he does not perceive feeling conditioned by gustatory contact.
He does not perceive feeling conditioned by bodily contact; he does not perceive feeling conditioned by mental contact.
He does not perceive the earth element.
He does not perceive the water element, he does not perceive the fire element,
he does not perceive the wind element.
He does not perceive the element of space;
he does not perceive the element of consciousness.
He does not perceive ignorance.
He does not perceive volitional formations; he does not perceive consciousness;
he does not perceive name-and-form.
He does not perceive the six sense bases; he does not perceive contact;
he does not perceive feeling.
One does not perceive craving,
one does not perceive grasping,
and one does not perceive becoming.
He does not perceive birth;
he does not perceive aging and death.
He does not perceive the perfection of generosity.
He does not perceive the perfection of ethical discipline; he does not perceive the perfection of patience;
he does not perceive the perfection of vigor.
He does not perceive the perfection of meditation;
he does not perceive the perfection of wisdom.
He does not perceive internal emptiness.
He does not perceive external emptiness;
he does not perceive internal-external emptiness;
he does not perceive the emptiness of emptiness.
He does not perceive great emptiness; he does not perceive the emptiness of the ultimate truth;
he does not perceive the emptiness of conditioned phenomena.
He does not perceive the emptiness of the unconditioned;
he does not perceive the emptiness of the ultimate;
he does not perceive the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end.
He does not perceive the emptiness of non-dispersal;
he does not perceive the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
he does not perceive the emptiness of all phenomena.
He does not perceive the emptiness of specific characteristics, he does not perceive the emptiness of non-apprehension,
and he does not perceive the emptiness of non-existence.
He does not perceive the emptiness of intrinsic nature; he does not perceive the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
he does not perceive the applications of mindfulness.
He does not perceive the right efforts; he does not perceive the bases of psychic power; he does not perceive the faculties; he does not perceive the powers.
He does not perceive [them]; he does not perceive the factors of enlightenment;
he does not perceive the noble eightfold path.
He does not perceive the noble truths; he does not perceive the meditative absorptions;
he does not perceive the immeasurables.
He does not perceive the formless attainments;
he does not perceive the eight liberations;
he does not perceive the nine successive meditative attainments.
He does not perceive the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
he does not perceive the superknowledges;
he does not perceive the meditative concentrations.
He does not perceive the gateways of dhāraṇī; he does not perceive the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
he does not perceive the four grounds of self-confidence.
He does not perceive the four analytical knowledges;
he does not perceive great loving-kindness;
he does not perceive great compassion.
He does not perceive the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
he does not perceive omniscience;
he does not perceive the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
One does not perceive omniscience.
Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of form is not form.
Thus, form and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of form is not form;
for in this way, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of feeling is not feeling.
Thus, feeling and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of feeling is not feeling.
Likewise, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of perception is not perception.
Thus, perception and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of perception is not perception.

For it is thus, Blessed One: that which is the non-arising of conditioned phenomena is not those conditioned phenomena; for conditioned phenomena and non-arising are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For it is thus, Blessed One: non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of formations is not those formations;
for likewise, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of consciousness is not that consciousness.
Thus, consciousness and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of consciousness is not consciousness.
For in this way, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the eye is not the eye.
Thus, the eye and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the eye is not the eye;
for likewise, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the ear is not the ear.
Thus, the ear and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
For thus, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the ear is not the ear.
Likewise, Blessed One, the non-arising of the nose is not the nose.
Thus, the nose and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the nose is not the nose.
For in this way, Blessed One, the non-arising of the tongue is not that tongue;
thus, the tongue and non-arising are non-dual, an undivided unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the tongue is not the tongue;
likewise, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the body is not the body.
For thus, the body and non-arising are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the body is not the body.
For likewise, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the mind is not the mind.
Thus, the mind and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the mind is not the mind.
"Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of form is not form;
for in this way, form and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of form is not form; that which is the non-arising of sound is not sound.
For sound and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of sound is not sound,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of odor is not odor.
Thus, fragrance and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of fragrance is not fragrance.
“Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of taste is not taste; for indeed, taste and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of taste is not taste;
O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of touch is not touch.
For touch and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of contact is not contact.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of phenomena is not those phenomena.
Thus, indeed, phenomena (*dharmas*) and non-arising (*anutpāda*) are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of phenomena is not those phenomena.
"Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of eye-consciousness is not that eye-consciousness;
for indeed, eye-consciousness and non-arising are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of eye-consciousness is not that eye-consciousness;
O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of ear-consciousness is not that ear-consciousness.
For indeed, ear-consciousness and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of auditory consciousness is not auditory consciousness,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of olfactory consciousness is not olfactory consciousness.
Thus, olfactory consciousness and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of olfactory consciousness is not that olfactory consciousness.
“Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of tongue-consciousness is not that tongue-consciousness; for indeed, tongue-consciousness and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of tongue-consciousness is not tongue-consciousness; that which is the non-arising of body-consciousness is not body-consciousness.
For body-consciousness and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of body-consciousness is not that body-consciousness,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of mind-consciousness is not that mind-consciousness.
Thus, mental consciousness and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of mental consciousness is not mental consciousness.
"Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of eye-contact is not eye-contact; for indeed, eye-contact and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of eye-contact is not eye-contact;
that which is the non-arising of ear-contact is not ear-contact.
For ear-contact and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of ear-contact is not ear-contact,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of nose-contact is not nose-contact.
Thus, indeed, olfactory contact and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of olfactory contact is not olfactory contact.
"Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of tongue-contact is not tongue-contact; for indeed, tongue-contact and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of tongue-contact is not tongue-contact;
that which is the non-arising of body-contact is not body-contact.
For body-contact and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of body-contact is not body-contact,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of mind-contact is not mind-contact.
Thus, mental contact and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of mental contact is not mental contact.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not that feeling conditioned by eye-contact;
for indeed, feeling conditioned by eye-contact and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not feeling conditioned by eye-contact;
that which is the non-arising of feeling conditioned by ear-contact is not feeling conditioned by ear-contact.
For indeed, feeling conditioned by ear-contact and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore,
that which is the non-arising of feeling conditioned by auditory contact is not itself the feeling conditioned by auditory contact.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of sensation conditioned by olfactory contact is not that sensation conditioned by olfactory contact;
for indeed, sensation conditioned by olfactory contact and non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of feeling conditioned by olfactory contact is not feeling conditioned by olfactory contact; that which is the non-arising of feeling conditioned by gustatory contact is not feeling conditioned by gustatory contact.
For indeed, feeling conditioned by gustatory contact and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of sensation conditioned by tongue-contact is not that sensation conditioned by tongue-contact.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of sensation conditioned by body-contact is not that sensation conditioned by body-contact.
Thus, the sensation conditioned by bodily contact and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the sensation conditioned by bodily contact is not that sensation conditioned by bodily contact.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of feeling conditioned by mental contact is not that feeling conditioned by mental contact;
for indeed, feeling conditioned by mental contact and non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of feeling conditioned by mental contact is not feeling conditioned by mental contact;
that which is the non-arising of the earth element is not the earth element.
For indeed, the earth element and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of the earth element is not the earth element,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of the water element is not the water element.
Thus, the water element and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the water element is not the water element.
O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the fire element is not the fire element; for indeed, the fire element and non-arising are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity.
For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the fire element is not the fire element.
O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the wind element is not the wind element;
for indeed, the wind element and non-arising are non-dual, this being an undivided unity. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the wind element is not the wind element;
O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the space element is not the space element.
For indeed, the space element and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of the space-element is not the space-element,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of the consciousness-element is not the consciousness-element.
Thus, indeed, the element of consciousness and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the element of consciousness is not the element of consciousness.
"Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of ignorance is not ignorance; for indeed, ignorance and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of ignorance is not ignorance; that which is the non-arising of formative forces is not those formative forces.
For indeed, formative forces and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of conditioned phenomena is not those conditioned phenomena.
“Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of consciousness is not consciousness; for indeed, consciousness and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of consciousness is not consciousness;
O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of name-and-form is not name-and-form.
For indeed, name-and-form and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of name-and-form is not name-and-form.
That which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of the six sense bases is not the six sense bases.
Thus, the six sense bases and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the six sense bases is not the six sense bases.
“Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of contact is not contact; for contact and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of contact is not contact;
that which, O Blessed One, is the non-arising of feeling is not feeling. For feeling and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of feeling is not that feeling,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of craving is not that craving.
Thus, craving and non-arising are non-dual; this is not a state of duality. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of craving is not craving.
"Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of grasping is not grasping; for grasping and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of grasping is not grasping;
O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of existence is not existence.
For indeed, existence and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of existence is not existence,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of birth is not birth.
For thus, birth and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of birth is not birth.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of old age and death is not old age and death; for indeed, old age and death and non-arising are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of aging and death is not aging and death;
that which is the non-arising of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity.
For indeed, the perfection of generosity and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of the perfection of ethical discipline is not the perfection of ethical discipline.
Thus, the perfection of ethical discipline and non-arising are non-dual; this is an undivided unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of ethical discipline is not the perfection of ethical discipline.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of patience is not the perfection of patience;
for indeed, the perfection of patience and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of patience is not the perfection of patience;
that which is the non-arising of the perfection of vigor is not the perfection of vigor.
For indeed, the perfection of vigor and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of vigor is not the perfection of vigor,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of the perfection of meditation is not the perfection of meditation.
Thus, indeed, the perfection of meditation and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of meditation is not the perfection of meditation.
“Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of wisdom is not the perfection of wisdom;
for indeed, the perfection of wisdom and non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the perfection of wisdom is not the perfection of wisdom;
that which is the non-arising of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness.
For indeed, internal emptiness and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness itself,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of external emptiness is not external emptiness itself.
Thus, indeed, external emptiness and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of external emptiness is not [itself] external emptiness.

O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of internal-and-external emptiness is not internal-and-external emptiness; for internal-and-external emptiness and non-arising are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of internal-and-external emptiness is not internal-and-external emptiness;
that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of emptiness is not the emptiness of emptiness.
For indeed, the emptiness of emptiness and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore,
that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of emptiness is not that emptiness of emptiness,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of great emptiness is not that great emptiness.
Thus, indeed, great emptiness and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of great emptiness is not [itself] great emptiness.
"Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of ultimate emptiness is not [itself] ultimate emptiness;
for ultimate emptiness and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of ultimate emptiness is not ultimate emptiness;
that which is the non-arising of conditioned emptiness is not conditioned emptiness.
For indeed, conditioned emptiness and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?

For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of the conditioned is not the emptiness of the conditioned,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of the emptiness of the unconditioned is not the emptiness of the unconditioned.
Thus, indeed, unconditioned emptiness and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of unconditioned emptiness is not [itself] unconditioned emptiness.
“Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of absolute emptiness is not itself absolute emptiness; for indeed, absolute emptiness and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”

Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of absolute emptiness is not absolute emptiness; that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is not the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end.
For indeed, the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is not itself the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of non-dispersal is not itself the emptiness of non-dispersal.
Thus, indeed, non-repudiation-emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*) and non-arising (*anutpāda*) are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of non-repudiation-emptiness is not itself non-repudiation-emptiness.
"Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of intrinsic emptiness is not that intrinsic emptiness;
for indeed, intrinsic emptiness and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not that emptiness of intrinsic nature;
that which, O Blessed One, is the non-arising of the emptiness of all phenomena is not that emptiness of all phenomena.
For indeed, the emptiness of all phenomena and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of all phenomena is not that emptiness of all phenomena.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of specific characteristics is not that emptiness of specific characteristics.
Thus, indeed, the emptiness of specific characteristics and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of specific characteristics is not itself the emptiness of specific characteristics.
"O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of non-apprehension is not itself the emptiness of non-apprehension;
for indeed, the emptiness of non-apprehension and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of non-apprehension is not the emptiness of non-apprehension;
and that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of non-existence is not the emptiness of non-existence.
For indeed, the emptiness of non-existence and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?

For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of non-existence is not the emptiness of non-existence,
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
