Thus, intrinsic emptiness and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of intrinsic emptiness is not [itself] intrinsic emptiness.

"Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is not the emptiness of the nature of non-existence; for indeed, the emptiness of the nature of non-existence and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is not the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and that which is the non-arising of the applications of mindfulness is not those applications of mindfulness. For the applications of mindfulness and non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the applications of mindfulness is not those applications of mindfulness;
that which is the non-arising of the right efforts is not those right efforts. For the right efforts and non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the right efforts is not those right efforts; that which is the non-arising of the bases of psychic power is not those bases of psychic power. For these bases of psychic power and non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the bases of psychic power is not those bases of psychic power;
that which is the non-arising of the faculties is not those faculties. For the faculties and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the faculties is not those faculties;

that which is the non-arising of the powers is not those powers. For the powers and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that? Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the powers is not those powers;
that which is the non-arising of the factors of enlightenment is not those factors of enlightenment. For the factors of enlightenment and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the factors of enlightenment is not those factors of enlightenment;
that which is the non-arising of the noble eightfold path is not that noble eightfold path. For the noble eightfold path and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the noble eightfold path is not the noble eightfold path;
and that which, O Blessed One, is the non-arising of the noble truths is not those noble truths. For the noble truths and non-arising are non-dual, an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the noble truths is not those noble truths;

that which is the non-arising of the meditative absorptions is not those meditative absorptions. For the meditative absorptions and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that? Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*) is not those meditative absorptions; that which is the non-arising of the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) is not those immeasurables. For the immeasurables and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the immeasurables is not those immeasurables;
that which is the non-arising of the formless attainments is not those formless attainments. For the formless attainments and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two.
Why is that?
For it is thus, Blessed One: non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of the formless attainments is not those formless attainments;
and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of the liberations is not those liberations. For liberation and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the liberations is not those liberations.

Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the successive meditative attainments is not those successive meditative attainments; for these successive meditative attainments and non-arising are non-dual.
It is non-dual. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling is not those successive attainments of meditative dwelling.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not those gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
For the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, and non-arising, are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not those gateways to liberation; that which is the non-arising of the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) is not those superknowledges. For indeed, the superknowledges and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the superknowledges is not those superknowledges;

that which is the non-arising of the meditative concentrations is not those meditative concentrations. For indeed, the meditative concentrations and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of concentrations is not those concentrations; that which is the non-arising of the gateways of dhāraṇīs is not those gateways of dhāraṇīs. For these gateways of dhāraṇīs and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the gateways of dhāraṇī is not those gateways of dhāraṇī;

that which is the non-arising of the ten powers of a Tathāgata is not those ten powers of a Tathāgata. For these ten powers of a Tathāgata and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. This is because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the ten powers of a Tathāgata is not those ten powers of a Tathāgata; and that which is the non-arising of the grounds of self-confidence is not those grounds of self-confidence. For indeed, the grounds of self-confidence and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that? Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the grounds of self-confidence is not those grounds of self-confidence;

and that which is the non-arising of the analytical knowledges is not those analytical knowledges. For indeed, the analytical knowledges and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that? Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) is not those analytical knowledges; that which is the non-arising of great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) is not that great loving-kindness. For indeed, great loving-kindness and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of great loving-kindness is not great loving-kindness; that which is the non-arising of great compassion is not great compassion.
For indeed, great compassion and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of great compassion is not great compassion;

and that which, Blessed One, is the non-arising of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not those unique qualities of a Buddha. For these unique qualities of a Buddha and non-arising are non-dual, and there is no division between them.
For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the unique qualities of a Buddha is not those unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of suchness is not suchness;
for suchness and non-arising are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of suchness is not suchness; that which is the non-arising of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is not that nature of phenomena.
For indeed, the nature of phenomena and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the true nature (*dharmatā*) is not that true nature.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is not that realm of phenomena.
For thus, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) and non-arising (*anutpāda*) are non-dual and not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the realm of phenomena is not the realm of phenomena.
“Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the fixed nature of phenomena is not the fixed nature of phenomena;
for indeed, the fixed nature of phenomena and non-arising are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the fixed order of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*) is not the fixed order of phenomena; and that which is the non-arising of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is not the limit of reality. For the limit of reality and non-arising are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the limit of reality is not the limit of reality;
that which is the non-arising of the inconceivable realm is not the inconceivable realm.
For indeed, the inconceivable realm and non-arising are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the inconceivable realm is not the inconceivable realm itself.
And, Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of omniscience is not omniscience itself.
For thus, omniscience and non-arising are non-dual and not divided into two;
why is that?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of omniscience is not omniscience; that which is the non-arising of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
For indeed, the knowledge of the aspects of the path and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the non-arising of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
Blessed One, that which is the non-arising of the knowledge of all aspects is not the knowledge of all aspects.
Thus, omniscience and non-arising are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the non-arising of omniscience is not omniscience itself.
“Blessed One, that which is the cessation of form is not form;
for form and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the passing away of form is not form; that which is the passing away of feeling is not feeling.
For in this way, feeling and its passing away are non-dual, being indivisible. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of feeling is not feeling,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of perception is not perception.
For thus, designation and cessation are non-dual and not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of perception is not that perception;
that which is the cessation of volitional formations is not those volitional formations.
For indeed, volitional formations and their cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of formations is not those formations.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of consciousness is not that consciousness.
Thus, consciousness and its passing away are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of consciousness is not consciousness itself.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the eye is not the eye;
for indeed, the eye and its cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of the eye is not the eye;
that which, O Blessed One, is the passing away of the ear is not the ear.
For indeed, the ear and its passing away are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of the ear is not the ear,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the nose is not the nose.
For in this way, the nose and its cessation are non-dual and not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the nose is not the nose.
"O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the tongue is not the tongue;
for indeed, the tongue and cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the disintegration of the tongue is not the tongue; that which is the disintegration of the body is not the body.
For indeed, the body and its disintegration are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of the body is not the body,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the mind is not the mind.
Thus, indeed, mind and passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of the mind is not the mind.
O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of form is not form; for form and cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of form is not form.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of sound is not sound; for sound and cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, that which is the passing away of sound is not sound;
that which, Blessed One, is the passing away of odor is not odor. For odor and its passing away are non-dual, an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of odor is not odor,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of taste is not taste.
Thus, indeed, taste and its passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of taste is not taste.
“Blessed One, that which is the cessation of contact is not contact;
for contact and cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, that which is the cessation of contact is not contact;
O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of phenomena is not those phenomena.
For indeed, phenomena and their cessation are non-dual, being without division.
For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of phenomena is not those phenomena.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of eye-consciousness is not that eye-consciousness;
for indeed, eye-consciousness and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the cessation of eye-consciousness is not that eye-consciousness; that which is the cessation of ear-consciousness is not that ear-consciousness.
For thus, ear-consciousness and its cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of auditory consciousness is not auditory consciousness,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of olfactory consciousness is not olfactory consciousness.
Thus, indeed, olfactory consciousness and its cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of olfactory consciousness is not olfactory consciousness.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of tongue-consciousness is not that tongue-consciousness;
for indeed, tongue-consciousness and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the cessation of tongue-consciousness is not that tongue-consciousness;
that which is the cessation of body-consciousness is not that body-consciousness.
For body-consciousness and its cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore,
that which is the cessation of body-consciousness is not that body-consciousness,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of mind-consciousness is not that mind-consciousness.
Thus, mental consciousness and cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of mental consciousness is not mental consciousness.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of eye-contact is not eye-contact;
for indeed, eye-contact and cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of eye-contact is not eye-contact;
that which is the cessation of ear-contact is not ear-contact.
For ear-contact and its cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of ear-contact is not that ear-contact,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of nose-contact is not that nose-contact.
Thus, indeed, olfactory contact and its cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of olfactory contact is not olfactory contact.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of tongue-contact is not tongue-contact;
for indeed, tongue-contact and cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of tongue-contact is not tongue-contact;
that which is the cessation of body-contact is not body-contact.
For body-contact and its cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of bodily contact is not bodily contact,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of mental contact is not mental contact.
For thus, mental contact and its cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of mental contact is not mental contact.
"O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not that feeling conditioned by eye-contact;
for indeed, feeling conditioned by eye-contact and its cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not that feeling conditioned by eye-contact;
that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by ear-contact is not that feeling conditioned by ear-contact.
For indeed, feeling conditioned by ear-contact and its cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the feeling conditioned by ear-contact is not that feeling conditioned by ear-contact.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the feeling conditioned by nose-contact is not that feeling conditioned by nose-contact.
Thus, indeed, the sensation conditioned by olfactory contact and its cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of the sensation conditioned by olfactory contact is not that sensation conditioned by olfactory contact.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is not that feeling conditioned by tongue-contact;
for indeed, the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact and its cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is not that feeling conditioned by tongue-contact;
that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by body-contact is not that feeling conditioned by body-contact.
For indeed, feeling conditioned by body-contact and its cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by bodily contact is not that feeling conditioned by bodily contact; that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by mental contact is not that feeling conditioned by mental contact.
Thus, feeling conditioned by mental contact and its cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of feeling conditioned by mental contact is not itself feeling conditioned by mental contact.
Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of the earth element is not the earth element;
for indeed, the earth element and its exhaustion are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, exhaustion is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the earth element is not the earth element;
that which is the cessation of the water element is not the water element.
For the water element and its cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of the water element is not the water element,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the fire element is not the fire element.
For thus, the fire element and its cessation are non-dual and not divided into two;
why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of the fire element is not the fire element;
that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the wind element is not the wind element.
For indeed, the wind element and its cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the wind element is not the wind element.
That which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the space element is not the space element.
Thus, the space element and cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of the space element is not the space element.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the consciousness-element is not the consciousness-element;
for indeed, the consciousness-element and cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, that which is the cessation of the consciousness-element is not the consciousness-element.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of ignorance is not ignorance;
for thus, ignorance and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore,
that which is the cessation of ignorance is not ignorance,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of formative forces is not those formative forces.
Thus, indeed, conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) and their passing away (*vyaya*) are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of conditioned phenomena is not those conditioned phenomena themselves.
“Blessed One, that which is the cessation of consciousness is not consciousness;
for consciousness and cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, [consciousness] is thus.”
Cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore,
O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of consciousness is not consciousness,
and that which is the cessation of name-and-form is not name-and-form.
Thus, name-and-form and passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of name-and-form is not name-and-form.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the six sense-bases is not the six sense-bases;
for indeed, the six sense-bases and their cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the six sense bases is not the six sense bases; that which is the cessation of contact is not contact.
For contact and its cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of contact is not contact,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of feeling is not feeling.
Thus, feeling and its passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of feeling is not itself feeling.
“Blessed One, that which is the cessation of craving is not craving;
for indeed, craving and cessation are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of craving is not craving; that which is the exhaustion of clinging is not clinging. For clinging and exhaustion are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of appropriation is not appropriation.
That which, Blessed One, is the cessation of existence is not existence.
Thus, indeed, existence (*bhava*) and cessation (*vyaya*) are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of existence is not existence.
"O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of birth is not birth;
for indeed, birth and cessation are non-dual, an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, that which is the cessation of birth is not birth;
O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of old age and death is not old age and death.
For indeed, old age and death and their cessation are non-dual, without division. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of aging and death is not aging and death.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity.
Thus, the perfection of generosity and its exhaustion are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, exhaustion is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity; that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of ethical discipline is not the perfection of ethical discipline.
For indeed, the perfection of ethical discipline and its exhaustion are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore,
that which is the cessation of the perfection of ethical discipline is not the perfection of ethical discipline,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the perfection of patience is not the perfection of patience.
Thus, the perfection of patience and its cessation are non-dual; this is not a duality. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of the perfection of patience is not the perfection of patience.
"Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of vigor is not the perfection of vigor;
for indeed, the perfection of vigor and exhaustion are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, exhaustion is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of vigor is not the perfection of vigor; that which is the exhaustion of the perfection of meditation is not the perfection of meditation.
For indeed, the perfection of meditation and its exhaustion are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore,
that which is the cessation of the perfection of meditation is not the perfection of meditation,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the perfection of wisdom is not the perfection of wisdom.
For thus, the perfection of wisdom and passing away are non-dual; this is not a duality. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of the perfection of wisdom is not the perfection of wisdom.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness;
for internal emptiness and cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the passing away of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness;
that which is the passing away of external emptiness is not external emptiness.
For indeed, external emptiness and its passing away are non-dual; this is an undivided unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of external emptiness is not external emptiness.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of internal-and-external emptiness is not internal-and-external emptiness.
Thus, internal-external emptiness and cessation are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of internal-external emptiness is not internal-external emptiness.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of emptiness is not the emptiness of emptiness;
for indeed, the emptiness of emptiness and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of emptiness is not the emptiness of emptiness;
that which is the cessation of the great emptiness is not the great emptiness.
For indeed, the great emptiness and cessation are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of great emptiness is not great emptiness,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of ultimate emptiness is not ultimate emptiness.
Thus, indeed, ultimate emptiness and passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of ultimate emptiness is not ultimate emptiness itself.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of the conditioned is not the emptiness of the conditioned;
for indeed, the emptiness of the conditioned and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the passing away of the emptiness of the conditioned is not the emptiness of the conditioned; that which is the passing away of the emptiness of the unconditioned is not the emptiness of the unconditioned.
For indeed, the emptiness of the unconditioned and passing away are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of the unconditioned is not the emptiness of the unconditioned.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of absolute emptiness is not absolute emptiness.
For thus, absolute emptiness and passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of absolute emptiness is not absolute emptiness itself.
“Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is not itself the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end;
for indeed, the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”

Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is not the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; that which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-dispersal is not the emptiness of non-dispersal.
For indeed, the emptiness of non-dispersal and cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-dispersal is not the emptiness of non-dispersal.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
For thus, intrinsic emptiness and passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of intrinsic emptiness is not intrinsic emptiness itself.
“Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of all dharmas is not the emptiness of all dharmas;
for indeed, the emptiness of all dharmas and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of all phenomena is not the emptiness of all phenomena;
that which is the cessation of the emptiness of specific characteristics is not the emptiness of specific characteristics.
For indeed, the emptiness of specific characteristics and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, non-arising is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of self-characteristic is not the emptiness of self-characteristic.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-apprehension is not the emptiness of non-apprehension.
Thus, non-apprehension-emptiness and passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of non-apprehension-emptiness is not non-apprehension-emptiness itself.

“Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of non-existence is not the emptiness of non-existence; for indeed, the emptiness of non-existence and cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”

Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the passing away of the emptiness of non-existence is not the emptiness of non-existence; that which is the passing away of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
For indeed, the emptiness of intrinsic nature and passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is not the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Thus, indeed, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence and cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is not itself the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the applications of mindfulness is not those applications of mindfulness;
for the applications of mindfulness and their cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the passing away of the foundations of mindfulness is not those foundations of mindfulness;
that which is the passing away of the right efforts is not those right efforts. For indeed, the right efforts and their passing away are non-dual and cannot be divided. Why is that?
Because, O Blessed One, passing away is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the right efforts is not those right efforts; that which is the cessation of the bases of psychic power is not those bases of psychic power.
For indeed, the bases of psychic power and their cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the bases of psychic power is not those bases of psychic power, and that which is the cessation of the faculties is not those faculties.
Thus, the sense-faculties and their passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of the sense-faculties is not those sense-faculties.
“Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of the powers is not those powers;
for indeed, the powers and the exhaustion are non-dual and not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, exhaustion is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.”
Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of the powers is not those powers; that which is the exhaustion of the factors of awakening is not those factors of awakening.
For indeed, the factors of awakening and their exhaustion are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of the factors of enlightenment is not those factors of enlightenment;

and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the noble eightfold path is not that noble eightfold path. Thus, the noble eightfold path and cessation are non-dual and cannot be divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct; therefore, that which is the cessation of the noble eightfold path is not the noble eightfold path,
and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the noble truths is not those noble truths.
Thus, the noble truths and their passing away are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of the noble truths is not those noble truths themselves.

Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of the meditative absorptions is not those meditative absorptions; for the meditative absorptions and their exhaustion are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, exhaustion is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the exhaustion of the meditative absorptions—

Those are not the meditative absorptions, O Blessed One; that which is the exhaustion of the immeasurables is not those immeasurables. For the immeasurables and their exhaustion are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, exhaustion is neither one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of the immeasurables is not those immeasurables;
that which is the exhaustion of the formless attainments is not those formless attainments. For the formless attainments and their exhaustion are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, exhaustion is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the passing away of the formless attainments is not those formless attainments;
that which is the passing away of the liberations is not those liberations. For liberation and passing away are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, O Blessed One, that which is the passing away of the liberations is not those liberations; that which is the passing away of the nine successive meditative attainments is not those successive meditative attainments.
For indeed, the successive meditative attainments and their passing away are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling is not those successive attainments of meditative dwelling.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not those gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
For emptiness, the signless, and the wishless—the gateways to liberation—and cessation are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, the signless, and the wishless—is not those gateways to liberation themselves.
"Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the superknowledges is not those superknowledges;
for indeed, the superknowledges and cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct."

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the passing away of the superknowledges is not those superknowledges; that which is the passing away of the meditative concentrations is not those meditative concentrations.
For indeed, the meditative concentrations and their passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;

therefore, that which is the cessation of the concentrations is not those concentrations. Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the gateways of the dhāraṇīs is not those gateways of the dhāraṇīs; for the gateways of the dhāraṇīs and cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that? (ŚsP_II-1_195)
For it is thus, Blessed One: exhaustion is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the exhaustion of the gateways of dhāraṇī is not those gateways of dhāraṇī.

Blessed One, that which is the exhaustion of the ten powers of a Tathāgata is not those ten powers of a Tathāgata; for the ten powers of a Tathāgata and exhaustion are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the ten powers of a Tathāgata is not those ten powers of a Tathāgata.

Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the grounds of self-confidence is not those grounds of self-confidence; for the grounds of self-confidence and cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of the fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*) is not those fearlessnesses;

and that which, Blessed One, is the cessation of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) is not those analytical knowledges. For the analytical knowledges and cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the analytical knowledges is not those analytical knowledges.
That which, Blessed One, is the cessation of great loving-kindness is not that great loving-kindness.
Thus, great loving-kindness and its cessation are non-dual; they are not divided into two. For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the cessation of great loving-kindness is not great loving-kindness.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of great compassion is not great compassion;
for indeed, great compassion and cessation are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.

Therefore, Blessed One, that which is the cessation of great compassion is not great compassion; that which is the cessation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not those unique qualities of a Buddha.
For these unique qualities of a Buddha and their cessation are non-dual and indivisible. Why is that?
For thus, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) is not those unique qualities of a Buddha.
Blessed One, that which is the cessation of omniscience (sarvajñatā) is not that omniscience.
For thus, omniscience and passing away are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, passing away is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct.
Therefore, that which is the passing away of omniscience is not omniscience.
“Blessed One, that which is the cessation of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not the knowledge of the aspects of the path;
for indeed, the knowledge of the aspects of the path and cessation are non-dual, they are not divided into two. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct. Therefore, that which...”
The cessation of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not that knowledge of the aspects of the path;
O Blessed One, the cessation of the knowledge of all aspects is not that knowledge of all aspects.
For indeed, the knowledge of all aspects and cessation are non-dual; this is an undivided unity. Why is that?
For in this way, Blessed One, cessation is not one, nor two, nor many, nor distinct;
therefore, that which is the cessation of omniscience (sarvākārajñatā) is not omniscience.
